# =============================================================================
# Makefile - Custom KN5000 ROM Build System
# =============================================================================
# Build custom ROMs for the Technics KN5000 keyboard.
#
# Targets:
#   make          - Build ROM and create MAME ROM set
#   make build    - Build custom ROM only
#   make romset   - Create complete MAME ROM set with custom program ROM
#   make clean    - Remove build artifacts
#   make test     - Run in MAME emulator
#
# Requirements:
#   - ASL Macro Assembler (asl) and p2bin in ../tools/asl/
#   - MAME unidasm disassembler in ../tools/unidasm
#   - Original KN5000 ROMs in /mnt/shared/kn5000_original_roms/kn5000/
#   - MAME with kn5000 driver (for testing)
# =============================================================================

# Tool paths (relative to project root)
ASL_PATH := ../../tools/asl
ASL := $(ASL_PATH)/asl
P2BIN := $(ASL_PATH)/p2bin
UNIDASM := ../../tools/unidasm
EXTRACT_RESOURCES := python3 tools/extract_resources.py

# Game data directory (original Another World files)
GAME_DATA_DIR := game_data/MSDOS

# Assembler flags
# -L generates listing file, -olist specifies listing filename
ASL_FLAGS := -w -q -L

# Build output directory
BUILD_DIR := out

# Source files
MAIN_SRC := src/main.asm
INCLUDE_DIR := src/includes

# Shared code from disasm repository
DISASM_REPO := ../../kn5000-roms-disasm

# Output files
MAIN_ROM := $(BUILD_DIR)/custom_program.rom
MAIN_DISASM := $(BUILD_DIR)/custom_program.disasm

# =============================================================================
# Target selection: maincpu (default) or extension
# =============================================================================
TARGET ?= maincpu

ifeq ($(TARGET),maincpu)
  ASL_EXTRA := -D TARGET_MAINCPU
  P2BIN_RANGE := -r 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF
  ROM_SIZE := 2097152
else ifeq ($(TARGET),extension)
  ASL_EXTRA := -D TARGET_EXTENSION
  P2BIN_RANGE := -r 0x280000-0x2FFFFF
  ROM_SIZE := 524288
endif

# =============================================================================
# MAME ROM Set Configuration
# =============================================================================
# Original ROM location
ORIGINAL_ROMS := /mnt/shared/kn5000_original_roms/kn5000

# Output ROM set location (MAME-ready)
ROMSET_BASE := /mnt/shared/custom_kn5000_roms/anotherworld
ROMSET_DIR := $(ROMSET_BASE)/kn5000

# Files to copy from original ROM set (all required for MAME kn5000 driver)
ORIGINAL_ROM_FILES := \
	kn5000_subcpu_boot.ic30 \
	kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom \
	kn5000_table_data_rom_even.ic3 \
	kn5000_table_data_rom_odd.ic1 \
	kn5000_rhythm_data_rom.ic14 \
	kn5000_waveform_rom.ic307 \
	kn5000_custom_data_rom.ic19

# The program ROM that gets replaced with our custom build
PROGRAM_ROM_NAME := kn5000_v10_program.rom

# =============================================================================
# Default target - build everything including ROM set
# =============================================================================
.PHONY: all
all: romset
	@echo ""
	@echo "Build complete! (TARGET=$(TARGET))"
	@echo "ROM set ready at: $(ROMSET_DIR)/"
	@echo "Test with: make test"

# =============================================================================
# Convenience targets for specific build modes
# =============================================================================
.PHONY: maincpu extension
maincpu:
	$(MAKE) all TARGET=maincpu

extension:
	$(MAKE) all TARGET=extension

# =============================================================================
# Build custom ROM only (no ROM set creation)
# =============================================================================
.PHONY: build
build: $(BUILD_DIR) $(MAIN_ROM) $(MAIN_DISASM)
	@echo "Build complete: $(MAIN_ROM)"
	@echo "Symbols used:   $(SYMBOLS_USED)"
	@echo "Symbols unused: $(SYMBOLS_UNUSED)"
	@echo "Disassembly:    $(MAIN_DISASM)"

# =============================================================================
# Create build directory
# =============================================================================
$(BUILD_DIR):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)

# =============================================================================
# Generate bitmap assets from game resources
# =============================================================================
ASSET_FILES := src/another_world_logo.bin src/other_bitmap.bin

.PHONY: assets
assets: src/resources/resource-0x49.bin src/resources/resource-0x53.bin
	touch src/another_world_logo.bin
	touch src/other_bitmap.bin
	python src/resources_to_images.py src/resources/resource-0x53.bin src/another_world_logo.bin
	python src/resources_to_images.py src/resources/resource-0x49.bin src/other_bitmap.bin

src/another_world_logo.bin: src/resources/resource-0x53.bin src/resources_to_images.py
	touch src/another_world_logo.bin
	python src/resources_to_images.py src/resources/resource-0x53.bin src/another_world_logo.bin

src/other_bitmap.bin: src/resources/resource-0x49.bin src/resources_to_images.py
	touch src/other_bitmap.bin
	python src/resources_to_images.py src/resources/resource-0x49.bin src/other_bitmap.bin

# =============================================================================
# Build main program ROM
# =============================================================================
# Symbol/listing file output (ASL listing with symbol table)
LISTING_FILE := $(BUILD_DIR)/main.listing
SYMBOLS_USED := $(BUILD_DIR)/symbols.used
SYMBOLS_UNUSED := $(BUILD_DIR)/symbols.unused

$(BUILD_DIR)/main.p: $(MAIN_SRC) $(wildcard $(INCLUDE_DIR)/*.inc) $(wildcard src/*.asm) $(ASSET_FILES) | $(BUILD_DIR)
	$(ASL) $(ASL_FLAGS) $(ASL_EXTRA) -olist $(LISTING_FILE) -i $(INCLUDE_DIR) -i src -i $(DISASM_REPO) -i $(DISASM_REPO)/shared $(MAIN_SRC) -o $@
	@# Extract symbol table from listing, split into used and unused
	@grep -E "^[ *]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]* :" $(LISTING_FILE) | \
		sed 's/ *| */\n/g' | \
		grep -E " :" | \
		grep -v "^$$" | \
		sed 's/^ *//' | \
		grep -v "^\*" | \
		sort > $(SYMBOLS_USED)
	@grep -E "^[ *]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]* :" $(LISTING_FILE) | \
		sed 's/ *| */\n/g' | \
		grep -E " :" | \
		grep -v "^$$" | \
		sed 's/^ *//' | \
		grep "^\*" | \
		sed 's/^\*//' | \
		sort > $(SYMBOLS_UNUSED)
	@echo "Symbols: $$(wc -l < $(SYMBOLS_USED)) used, $$(wc -l < $(SYMBOLS_UNUSED)) unused"

$(MAIN_ROM): $(BUILD_DIR)/main.p
	$(P2BIN) $< $@ $(P2BIN_RANGE) -l 0xFF
	@# Verify ROM size
	@SIZE=$$(stat -c%s "$@" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$@" 2>/dev/null); \
	if [ "$$SIZE" -lt $(ROM_SIZE) ]; then \
		echo "Padding ROM to $(ROM_SIZE) bytes..."; \
		dd if=/dev/zero bs=1 count=$$(($(ROM_SIZE) - $$SIZE)) 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\377' >> $@; \
	fi
	@echo "ROM size: $$(stat -c%s "$@" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$@" 2>/dev/null) bytes"

# =============================================================================
# Generate reference disassembly using MAME's unidasm
# =============================================================================
$(MAIN_DISASM): $(MAIN_ROM)
	@echo "Generating reference disassembly..."
	$(UNIDASM) $< -arch tlcs900 -basepc 0xE00000 > $@

# =============================================================================
# Create complete MAME ROM set
# =============================================================================
.PHONY: romset
romset: $(MAIN_ROM)
	@echo "Creating MAME ROM set at $(ROMSET_DIR)/"
	@# Create ROM set directory
	mkdir -p $(ROMSET_DIR)
	@# Copy original ROM files
	@for rom in $(ORIGINAL_ROM_FILES); do \
		if [ -f "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)/$$rom" ]; then \
			cp "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)/$$rom" "$(ROMSET_DIR)/"; \
			echo "  Copied: $$rom"; \
		else \
			echo "  WARNING: Missing original ROM: $$rom"; \
		fi; \
	done
	@# Copy our custom ROM as the program ROM
	cp $(MAIN_ROM) $(ROMSET_DIR)/$(PROGRAM_ROM_NAME)
	@echo "  Installed: $(PROGRAM_ROM_NAME) (custom build)"
	@# Show ROM set contents
	@echo ""
	@echo "ROM set contents:"
	@ls -la $(ROMSET_DIR)/

# =============================================================================
# Clean build artifacts
# =============================================================================
.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)
	rm -f $(ASSET_FILES)
	@echo "Clean complete (ROM set at $(ROMSET_DIR) preserved)"

# Full clean including ROM set
.PHONY: distclean
distclean: clean
	rm -rf $(ROMSET_BASE)
	@echo "ROM set removed"

# =============================================================================
# Test in MAME
# =============================================================================
.PHONY: test
test: romset
	@echo ""
	@echo "Running MAME with custom ROM set..."
	@echo "ROM path: $(ROMSET_BASE)"
	@echo ""
	mame kn5000 -rompath $(ROMSET_BASE)

# Non-interactive test (just verify ROM loads)
.PHONY: test-verify
test-verify: romset
	@echo "Verifying ROM set with MAME..."
	mame kn5000 -rompath $(ROMSET_BASE) -verifyroms

# =============================================================================
# Development helpers
# =============================================================================

# Show hex dump of ROM
.PHONY: hexdump
hexdump: $(MAIN_ROM)
	hexdump -C $(MAIN_ROM) | head -100

# Show reset vector area
.PHONY: showvector
showvector: $(MAIN_ROM)
	@echo "Reset vector area (0xFFFEE0 = offset 0x1FFEE0):"
	hexdump -C $(MAIN_ROM) -s 0x1FFEE0 -n 32

# Verify assembler is available
.PHONY: check
check:
	@echo "Checking build tools..."
	@if [ -x "$(ASL)" ]; then \
		echo "  ASL: $(ASL)"; \
		$(ASL) -version 2>&1 | head -1 | sed 's/^/    /'; \
	else \
		echo "  ERROR: ASL not found at $(ASL)"; \
		exit 1; \
	fi
	@if [ -x "$(P2BIN)" ]; then \
		echo "  P2BIN: $(P2BIN)"; \
	else \
		echo "  ERROR: P2BIN not found at $(P2BIN)"; \
		exit 1; \
	fi
	@echo ""
	@echo "Checking original ROMs..."
	@if [ -d "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)" ]; then \
		echo "  Original ROM directory: $(ORIGINAL_ROMS)"; \
		for rom in $(ORIGINAL_ROM_FILES); do \
			if [ -f "$(ORIGINAL_ROMS)/$$rom" ]; then \
				echo "    OK: $$rom"; \
			else \
				echo "    MISSING: $$rom"; \
			fi; \
		done; \
	else \
		echo "  ERROR: Original ROM directory not found: $(ORIGINAL_ROMS)"; \
		exit 1; \
	fi

# =============================================================================
# Help
# =============================================================================
.PHONY: help
help:
	@echo "KN5000 Custom ROM Build System (Another World VM)"
	@echo ""
	@echo "Build targets:"
	@echo "  make          - Build maincpu ROM and create MAME ROM set (default)"
	@echo "  make maincpu  - Build as standalone main CPU ROM (2MB, for MAME)"
	@echo "  make extension- Build as HDAE5000 extension board ROM (512KB)"
	@echo "  make build    - Build custom ROM only (current TARGET)"
	@echo ""
	@echo "Other targets:"
	@echo "  make romset   - Create complete MAME ROM set"
	@echo "  make test     - Run in MAME emulator"
	@echo "  make clean    - Remove build artifacts (preserves ROM set)"
	@echo "  make distclean- Remove everything including ROM set"
	@echo "  make check    - Verify build tools and original ROMs"
	@echo "  make help     - Show this help"
	@echo ""
	@echo "Current TARGET: $(TARGET)"
	@echo ""
	@echo "Output locations:"
	@echo "  Build:   $(BUILD_DIR)/"
	@echo "  ROM set: $(ROMSET_DIR)/"
	@echo ""
	@echo "The ROM set can be used with MAME:"
	@echo "  mame kn5000 -rompath $(ROMSET_BASE)"

Everything works. Here's a summary of what was done:

**Makefile changes:**
- Added `EXTRACT_RESOURCES` tool path and `GAME_DATA_DIR` variable pointing to `game_data/MSDOS`
- Added `resources` target that runs `extract_resources.py` with a stamp file (`.extracted`) for dependency tracking
- Made `assets` target depend on `$(RESOURCE_STAMP)` instead of individual resource files, creating a proper chain: `resources` -> `assets` -> `build` -> `romset`
- Updated `clean` to remove the stamp file (resources themselves are preserved)
- Updated `help` to list the new target

**extract_resources.py changes:**
- Merges best data from 3 sources: bank extraction, pre-extracted `.bin` in game_data, and existing output files
- Never overwrites non-zero content with zero-filled data
- Shows `[SAME]`/`[KEEP]`/`[OK]`/`[ZERO]` status for each resource

**VM changes (completing the previous session):**
- Replaced all 3 remaining hardcoded `INTRO_VIDEO_*` references with dynamic pointers (`CUR_VIDEO_DATA`, `CUR_VIDEO_1`, `CUR_VIDEO_2`)
- Added `CUR_VIDEO_1` variable to hold the video1 address for reset after video2 use
- Removed unused `video` macro and legacy EQU aliases

; ====  LOAD instruction  ====
	CP A, 19h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_LOAD
	LD WA, (XIX)	; uint16_t resourceId = fetch_word()
	EX W, A			; byte-swap: bytecode is big-endian
	INC 2, XIX

	; resourceId == 0: stop sound (no-op, we don't have sound)
	CP WA, 0
	JP EQ, _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

	; resourceId > 0x91: part switch request
	CP WA, NUM_MEM_LIST
	JP ULE, _load_check_screen
	LD (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), WA
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

_load_check_screen:
	; Check if resourceId matches a known screen bitmap resource
	; screen_resource_indexes = {0x49, 0x53} (available resources)
	CP WA, 049h
	JP NE, _load_not_0x49
	LD XHL, SCREEN_BITMAP_0x49
	CALL LOAD_SCREEN
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
_load_not_0x49:
	CP WA, 053h
	JP NE, _load_unknown
	LD XHL, SCREEN_BITMAP_0x53
	CALL LOAD_SCREEN

; ====  BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER instruction  ====
	CP A, 10h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER
	LD A, (XIX)		; byte pageId

	PUSH WA			; save pageId
	LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
	CP WA, GAME_PART_INTRO
	JP NE, _blit_no_hack
	LD A, 067h
	CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vm_var[0x67]
	CP DE, 1
	JP NE, _blit_no_hack
	LD A, 0DCh
	LD DE, 021h
	CALL _write_vm_var
_blit_no_hack:
	POP WA			; restore pageId (A = pageId)
	CALL UPDATE_DISPLAY
	CALL PAUSE			; Frame timing delay

I see a critical issue. When `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS` detects a part switch at line 1192-1196:

```asm
LD WA, (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART)
CP WA, 0
JP EQ, _no_part_switch
; Part switch requested - call initForPart
CALL initForPart
LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
```

But `initForPart` reads `CURRENT_PART_ID`:
```asm
LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
SUB WA, GAME_PART_FIRST


```

The problem is that `CURRENT_PART_ID` is never updated! When the intro requests a switch to the water part (0x3E82), `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART` is set to 0x3E82, but `initForPart` reads `CURRENT_PART_ID` which is still 0x3E81 (intro). The new part ID from `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART` needs to be stored into `CURRENT_PART_ID` before calling `initForPart`. Let me check the reference implementation to confirm this pattern.

Looking at the reference C++ code, it sets `m_currentPart = part` before calling `initForPart`. Our code is missing that step—we need to load the requested part ID and store it into `CURRENT_PART_ID` before the `initForPart` call, then clear the request flag afterward.

```

LD WA, (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART)
CP WA, 0
JP EQ, _no_part_switch
LD (CURRENT_PART_ID), WA    ; ← missing line
CALL initForPart
LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
```

But wait—`GAME_RESET` has the same issue. It loads the part ID into WA and calls `initForPart`, but `initForPart` immediately overwrites WA by reading from `CURRENT_PART_ID`. So `GAME_RESET` also needs to set `CURRENT_PART_ID` before calling `initForPart`.

1→# MAME Driver Source Files
     2→
     3→This directory contains a subset of MAME source files for the KN5000 driver. These are **reference copies** used for sketching driver improvements - NOT the complete MAME codebase.
     4→
     5→## Purpose
     6→
     7→These files serve as a workspace for:
     8→1. Planning control panel HLE (High Level Emulation) improvements
     9→2. Designing protocol implementations based on reverse engineering findings
    10→3. Drafting code changes before submitting to upstream MAME
    11→
    12→## Files
    13→
    14→| File | Description |
    15→|------|-------------|
    16→| `src/mame/matsushita/kn5000.cpp` | Main KN5000 driver - machine configuration, address maps, ROM definitions |
    17→| `src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.cpp` | Control panel HLE device implementation |
    18→| `src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` | Control panel HLE device header |
    19→
    20→## KN5000 Driver Architecture
    21→
    22→The MAME driver emulates:
    23→
    24→- **Main CPU**: TMP94C241F (TLCS-900/H2) at 20 MHz
    25→- **Sub CPU**: Second TMP94C241F
    26→- **Control Panel**: HLE device (no MCU ROM dumps available)
    27→- **Memory**: 16MB address space with ROM, RAM, and I/O regions
    28→- **Serial**: UART communication between main CPU and control panel
    29→
    30→### Control Panel HLE (`kn5000_cpanel_device`)
    31→
    32→The control panel uses High Level Emulation because the Mitsubishi M37471M2196S MCUs do not have ROM dumps available. The HLE device:
    33→
    34→- Implements serial communication via shift registers (RX and TX)
    35→- Uses a timer-driven baud rate generator (31,250 Hz default during init, 250 kHz normal operation)
    36→- Provides callbacks for TXD (transmit data) and SCLK (serial clock) signals
    37→- Sends initial command 0xE2 on startup (matches firmware expectations)
    38→
    39→### Communication Protocol
    40→
    41→The main CPU communicates with the control panel via serial at address `0x120000` (latch registers). The protocol uses:
    42→
    43→- **Commands**: E1, E2, E3, 00-1F (see control-panel-protocol.md in kn5000-docs)
    44→- **Responses**: Button states, encoder values, acknowledgments
    45→- **Packet types**: Single-byte, multi-byte, and special encoder packets
    46→
    47→## Workflow
    48→
    49→1. **Study**: Analyze reverse engineering findings from the disassembly
    50→2. **Design**: Draft improvements to HLE based on protocol understanding
    51→3. **Implement**: Update these reference files with proposed changes
    52→4. **Test**: Build MAME with the modified driver and test
    53→5. **Submit**: Create pull request to upstream MAME repository
    54→
    55→## Related Documentation
    56→
    57→- `../kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` - Complete protocol analysis
    58→- `../kn5000-docs/memory-map.md` - Hardware register addresses
    59→- `../maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm` - Main CPU disassembly (control panel routines at FC4xxx)
    60→
    61→## License
    62→
    63→These files are from MAME and are licensed under GPL-2.0-or-later. See individual file headers for copyright information.
    64→

1→; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>
     2→; Licensed under GPL version 2 or later.
     3→;
     4→; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
     5→; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
     6→; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
     7→;
     8→; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
     9→;
    10→; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
    11→; as a high-level emulation on MAME
    12→;
    13→; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
    14→; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
    15→;
    16→; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
    17→; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
    18→;
    19→; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
    20→; using the scripts provided at:
    21→; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
    22→;
    23→; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
    24→PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
    25→REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
    26→INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
    27→DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
    28→NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh
    29→TICKS_PER_SLICE		EQU 250		; ~20ms at 12500 Hz tick rate (80 µs/tick)
    30→
    31→CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
    32→REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte
    33→
    34→FROZEN	EQU 0
    35→NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
    36→NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh
    37→
    38→; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
    39→; MAINCPU: in DRAM at 0x020000-0x05FFFF
    40→; EXTENSION: in extension board SRAM at 0x240000-0x27FFFF
    41→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
    42→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 020000h
    43→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 030000h
    44→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 040000h
    45→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 050000h
    46→	endif
    47→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
    48→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
    49→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
    50→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
    51→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h
    52→	endif
    53→
    54→; VM variable indices (used by the game engine)
    55→VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED		EQU 03Ch
    56→VM_VARIABLE_LAST_KEYCHAR	EQU 0C5h
    57→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN	EQU 0E5h
    58→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN	EQU 0DCh
    59→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT	EQU 0E9h
    60→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK	EQU 0FAh
    61→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION		EQU 0FBh
    62→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK EQU 0FBh
    63→VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y		EQU 0F9h
    64→
    65→; Game part IDs (from reference: parts.h)
    66→GAME_PART_FIRST			EQU 03E80h
    67→GAME_PART_PROTECTION	EQU 03E80h	; Part 0: Copy protection
    68→GAME_PART_INTRO			EQU 03E81h	; Part 1: Introduction cinematic
    69→GAME_PART_WATER			EQU 03E82h	; Part 2: Water / lake
    70→GAME_PART_JAIL			EQU 03E83h	; Part 3: Jail / prison
    71→GAME_PART_CITADEL		EQU 03E84h	; Part 4: Citadel
    72→GAME_PART_BATTLECHAR	EQU 03E85h	; Part 5: Battle cinematic
    73→GAME_PART_ARENA			EQU 03E86h	; Part 6: Arena
    74→GAME_PART_FINAL			EQU 03E87h	; Part 7: Final / ending
    75→GAME_PART_PASSWORD1		EQU 03E88h	; Part 8: Password entry
    76→GAME_PART_PASSWORD2		EQU 03E89h	; Part 9: Password entry (alt)
    77→GAME_PART_LAST			EQU 03E89h
    78→GAME_NUM_PARTS			EQU 10
    79→NUM_MEM_LIST			EQU 091h
    80→
    81→CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN:
    82→	; int16_t xmax = MAX(x1, x2);
    83→	LD WA, (X1)
    84→	CP WA, (X2)
    85→	JP GT, XMAX_OK
    86→	LD WA, (X2)
    87→XMAX_OK:
    88→	LD (LINE_XMAX), WA
    89→	
    90→	; int16_t xmin = MIN(x1, x2);
    91→	LD WA, (X1)
    92→	CP WA, (X2)
    93→	JP LT, XMIN_OK
    94→	LD WA, (X2)
    95→XMIN_OK:
    96→	LD (LINE_XMIN), WA
    97→	RET
    98→
    99→drawLineN:
   100→	; Inputs:
   101→	; C = color
   102→	PUSH XIX
   103→	PUSH XHL
   104→	
   105→	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN
   106→
   107→	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
   108→	; 	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = color;
   109→	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
   110→	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   111→	EXTS XHL
   112→	ADD XIX, XHL
   113→	LD HL, (LINE_XMAX)
   114→	SUB HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   115→	INC HL				; inclusive range: xmax-xmin+1 pixels
   116→
   117→drawLineN_loop:
   118→	LDB (XIX), C
   119→	INC XIX
   120→	DJNZ HL, drawLineN_loop
   121→	
   122→	POP XHL
   123→	POP XIX
   124→	RET
   125→
   126→drawLineP:
   127→	; Copy pixels from PAGE_BITMAP_0 to curPagePtr1
   128→	PUSH XIX
   129→	PUSH XIY
   130→	PUSH XHL
   131→
   132→	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN
   133→
   134→	; Destination: CUR_LINE + LINE_XMIN (in curPagePtr1)
   135→	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
   136→	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   137→	EXTS XHL
   138→	ADD XIX, XHL
   139→
   140→	; Source: PAGE_BITMAP_0 + HLINEY*320 + LINE_XMIN
   141→	LD XIY, PAGE_BITMAP_0
   142→	LD XWA, 0
   143→	LD WA, (HLINEY)
   144→	LD DE, 320
   145→	MUL XWA, DE
   146→	ADD XIY, XWA
   147→	LD XHL, 0
   148→	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   149→	EXTS XHL
   150→	ADD XIY, XHL

1→# Code Review: KN5000 Another World VM Port
     2→
     3→## Comparison with reference MAME HLE implementation
     4→
     5→Reference commit: https://github.com/felipesanches/mame/commit/7cbb93bc3ee05f5ffdd083081530ac0daa2dfa84
     6→
     7→### Fully Implemented
     8→- **Opcode 0x00** (movConst) - OK
     9→- **Opcode 0x04** (CALL) - OK
    10→- **Opcode 0x05** (RET) - OK
    11→- **Opcode 0x06** (pauseThread/BREAK) - OK
    12→- **Opcode 0x07** (JMP) - OK
    13→- **Opcode 0x08** (setVect) - OK
    14→- **Opcode 0x09** (DJNZ) - OK
    15→- **Opcode 0x0B** (setPalette) - OK
    16→- **Opcode 0x0D** (selectVideoPage) - OK
    17→- **Opcode 0x0E** (fillVideoPage) - OK
    18→- **Opcode 0x10** (blitFramebuffer) - OK (missing pause-slices timing, but functional)
    19→- **Opcode 0x11** (killThread) - OK
    20→- **Opcode 0x80** (video instruction high bit) - OK
    21→- Polygon rendering pipeline (readVertices, fillPolygon, calcStep, readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy) - OK
    22→- Thread scheduler (NEXT_THREAD, CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS) - OK
    23→- Video page management (GET_PAGE_PTR, UPDATE_DISPLAY, VIDEO_START) - OK
    24→- Character/string drawing - OK
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→### Critical Missing/Broken Items
    29→
    30→#### 1. **Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - BUG: doesn't actually copy the value**
    31→(`another_world_vm.asm:1148-1165`)
    32→
    33→The MOV instruction reads `srcVariableId` and `dstVariableId` but the write at line 1163 writes to `XIY` which still points to `VM_VARIABLES + srcVariableId`, not `dstVariableId`. The `POP WA` on line 1162 restores dstVariableId, but XIY is never recalculated to point at it. The variable index in XWA is never used to recompute the destination address.
    34→
    35→#### 2. **Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - BUG: same as MOV, doesn't add**
    36→(`another_world_vm.asm:1168-1186`)
    37→
    38→This is literally a copy of MOV's code. It reads the source value but never adds it to the destination. It should: read dst value, read src value, add them, write back to dst.
    39→
    40→#### 3. **Opcode 0x03 (addConst) - Endianness bug**
    41→(`another_world_vm.asm:1189-1203`)
    42→
    43→The `fetch_word()` at line 1199 reads 2 bytes from the bytecode. But the reference uses big-endian reads (`READ_WORD_AW` = `READ_BYTE(A) << 8 | READ_BYTE(A+1)`), while `LD WA, (XIX)` reads in native little-endian order. The bytecode is big-endian (Amiga/68k origin). **This same endianness issue likely affects all `fetch_word()` operations throughout the code** (opcodes 0x00, 0x03, 0x04, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, etc.).
    44→
    45→#### 4. **Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    46→(`another_world_vm.asm:1316-1325`)
    47→
    48→This just skips 5 bytes and does nothing. The conditional jump is essential for all game logic (branches, comparisons). Without it, the game can only run linear sequences. The reference has 6 comparison modes (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le) plus variable-length operands depending on subopcode bits 6-7.
    49→
    50→#### 5. **Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    51→(`another_world_vm.asm:1339-1344`)
    52→
    53→Doesn't even consume its 3 bytes of arguments (first, last, type). This will desynchronize the bytecode parser, causing every subsequent instruction to decode incorrectly. The reference implementation freezes/unfreezes/deletes ranges of threads.
    54→
    55→#### 6. **Opcode 0x0F (copyVideoPage) - Ignores vscroll parameter**
    56→(`another_world_vm.asm:1379-1399`)
    57→
    58→The reference reads `VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y` and supports vertical scrolling with source/dest Y offsets. The KN5000 version does a plain memcpy. Also ignores the conditional `srcPageId & 0x80` / `srcPageId & 0xBF` logic for special scroll behavior.
    59→
    60→#### 7. **Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    61→(`another_world_vm.asm:1427-1431`)
    62→
    63→Doesn't consume its 5 bytes of arguments (word stringId, byte x, byte y, byte color). Will desync the bytecode stream. The DRAW_STRING routine exists but is never called from here.
    64→
    65→#### 8. **Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    66→(`another_world_vm.asm:1434-1439`)
    67→
    68→Doesn't consume its 2 bytes. Will desync.
    69→
    70→#### 9. **Opcode 0x14 (AND) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    71→(`another_world_vm.asm:1442-1447`)
    72→
    73→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    74→
    75→#### 10. **Opcode 0x15 (OR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    76→(`another_world_vm.asm:1450-1455`)
    77→
    78→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    79→
    80→#### 11. **Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    81→(`another_world_vm.asm:1458-1463`)
    82→
    83→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    84→
    85→#### 12. **Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    86→(`another_world_vm.asm:1466-1471`)
    87→
    88→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    89→
    90→#### 13. **Opcode 0x19 (LOAD/updateMemList) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    91→(`another_world_vm.asm:1484-1490`)
    92→
    93→Skips the word argument but does nothing. In the reference, this handles:
    94→- `resourceId == 0`: stop all sound
    95→- `resourceId > 0x91`: switch to a new game part (level change)
    96→- Otherwise: load a screen bitmap resource
    97→
    98→#### 14. **Opcode 0x40 (video with extended addressing) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    99→(`another_world_vm.asm:1072-1125`)
   100→
   101→The entire opcode 0x40 block is commented out and jumps to end without consuming any bytes. This handles polygon rendering with variable X/Y addressing modes and zoom. It's required for most in-game polygon graphics. **The variable-length encoding means skipping an unknown number of bytes, so this will definitely desync the VM.**
   102→
   103→#### 15. **drawLineP - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
   104→(`another_world_vm.asm:89-102`)
   105→
   106→Should copy pixels from page_bitmaps[0] to curPagePtr1, but just draws solid color.
   107→
   108→#### 16. **drawLineBlend - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
   109→(`another_world_vm.asm:104-117`)
   110→
   111→Should read the existing pixel and apply `(color & 7) | 8`, but just draws solid color.
   112→
   113→#### 17. **INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
   114→(`another_world_vm.asm:908-910`)
   115→
   116→Returns immediately. Without input handling, the game can never be interactive. The reference reads button/keyboard state and sets ~8 VM variables for hero movement, action, and mask.
   117→
   118→#### 18. **LOAD_SCREEN - Hardcoded to single bitmap**
   119→(`another_world_vm.asm:747-753`)
   120→
   121→Ignores the `screen_id` parameter entirely. The reference has 12 screen resources that get selected by index. Only one bitmap is ever loaded.
   122→
   123→#### 19. **Part/level switching not implemented**
   124→The reference has `initForPart()` / `setupPart()` which bank-switches bytecode, palettes, and video data when the game transitions between parts (intro, lake, jail, etc.). The KN5000 port hardcodes `INTRO_BYTECODE`, `INTRO_PALETTES`, `INTRO_VIDEO_1` labels, with no bank switching. `m_requestedNextPart` checking is commented out in `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS`.
   125→
   126→#### 20. **VM hacks not implemented**
   127→The reference has several critical hacks:
   128→- `VM_HACK_SWITCH_FROM_INTRO_TO_LAKE`: Sets var 0xDC when transitioning from intro
   129→- `VM_HACK_INIT_VAR_54_WITH_81`: Required for the Interplay logo to show
   130→- `VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED`: Never initialized (noted as TODO on line 228)
   131→
   132→---
   133→
   134→### Summary by Severity
   135→
   136→**Will crash/desync the VM** (bytecode not consumed correctly):
   137→- Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - missing 3 bytes
   138→- Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - missing 5 bytes
   139→- Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - missing 2 bytes
   140→- Opcode 0x14 (AND) - missing 3 bytes
   141→- Opcode 0x15 (OR) - missing 3 bytes
   142→- Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - missing 3 bytes
   143→- Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - missing 3 bytes
   144→- Opcode 0x40 (video extended) - variable length, unparsed
   145→- Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - skips 5 bytes, but actual length is variable (5-6 bytes depending on subopcode)
   146→
   147→**Wrong behavior (logic bugs):**
   148→- Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - writes to wrong variable
   149→- Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - doesn't add, just copies (also to wrong dest)
   150→- Big-endian fetch_word not handled (affects most word-reading opcodes)
   151→
   152→**Missing but won't desync:**
   153→- Input handling
   154→- Part/level switching
   155→- Sound (understandable given hardware constraints)
   156→
   157→The port currently can only play the intro cinematic in a linear fashion (no branching, no interaction). To reach "complete and functional" status, the highest priority items would be: fixing the endianness issue, implementing condJmp (0x0A), fixing MOV/ADD, implementing the bytecode-consuming stubs to prevent desync, and then implementing opcode 0x40 for full polygon rendering.
   158→

1→# Code Review: Polygon Rendering Glitches (2026-02-10)
     2→
     3→Thorough review of `src/another_world_vm.asm` against the reference C++ implementation
     4→([Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM](https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter/blob/master/src/video.cpp)).
     5→
     6→## Bug #1: `drawPoint` clobbers x coordinate (DEFINITE BUG)
     7→
     8→**Location:** `drawPoint` lines 184-196
     9→
    10→**Problem:** `LD DE, 320` overwrites DE, which held the x coordinate. Then `EXTZ XDE`
    11→zero-extends 320 (not x), and `ADD XWA, XDE` computes `y*320 + 320` instead of `y*320 + x`.
    12→
    13→Every single-pixel point is drawn at the wrong x position.
    14→
    15→**Fix:** Save DE (x) before loading 320 into DE for multiply, restore after.
    16→
    17→## Bug #2: Opcode 0x40 zoom case 3 — video2 not selected (WRONG POLYGONS)
    18→
    19→**Location:** `_0x40_zoom_case3` (line ~1391) and `readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy` (line ~863)
    20→
    21→**Problem:** The reference sets `m_useSegVideo2 = true` for zoom case 3, using video2 as the
    22→polygon data source. Our code always uses `INTRO_VIDEO_1`. The `INTRO_VIDEO_2` data IS
    23→available (bincluded), just never referenced.
    24→
    25→Both places that resolve polygon data pointers are affected:
    26→- Opcode 0x40 handler: `LD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_1`
    27→- Hierarchy function: `ADD XIX, INTRO_VIDEO_1`
    28→
    29→**Fix:** Add a `CUR_VIDEO_DATA` variable (DD), default to `INTRO_VIDEO_1`, set to
    30→`INTRO_VIDEO_2` in zoom case 3. Reference it in both the 0x40 handler and hierarchy.
    31→Reset back to VIDEO_1 after the opcode completes.
    32→
    33→## Bug #3: `readVertices` uses signed shift on unsigned product (LATENT)
    34→
    35→**Location:** `readVertices` and `readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy` — all `SRAW 6, WA` occurrences
    36→
    37→**Problem:** `SRAW 6, WA` performs a signed arithmetic shift right. The product `byte * zoom`
    38→is unsigned (0 to 65025). When the product exceeds 32767 (bit 15 set), SRAW sign-extends,
    39→giving a wrong negative result.
    40→
    41→**Impact:** Only manifests when `byte * zoom > 32767`, i.e., zoom > 128 with large vertex
    42→bytes. For the default zoom 0x40 (64), max product is 255 * 64 = 16320, well under 32767.
    43→**Harmless for the intro** but would be wrong for later game parts with non-default zoom.
    44→
    45→**Fix (for future):** Use `SRL 2, XWA` + `SRL 4, XWA` (shift 32-bit result right by 6
    46→unsigned) instead of `SRAW 6, WA`.
    47→
    48→## Verified Correct (no issues found)
    49→
    50→- `CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN` — correct signed comparison and sort
    51→- `fillPolygon` clipping — matches reference bounds checks exactly
    52→- `calcStep` — correct DIV/MULS/SLA logic, parameter order matches reference
    53→- `readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy` — stack frame offsets all verified correct
    54→- `CPT1/CPT2` 32-bit addition with carry — carry preserved across `LD` (flags unaffected)
    55→- CUR_LINE recomputed each segment from HLINEY — incremental +320 is correct
    56→- Draw function pointer (XHL) preserved by PUSH/POP across draw calls
    57→- Color (C register) preserved through fillPolygon raster loop for drawLineN case
    58→- Thread management (NEXT_THREAD, CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS) — correct
    59→

## Part Switching Implementation in KN5000 Another World ROM

I found the part switching code in the custom KN5000 Another World ROM. Here's how it works:

### Overview

The part switching is implemented through:
1. **Opcode 0x19 (LOAD/updateMemList)** - Requests a part switch
2. **initForPart()** function - Handles the actual part switch
3. **CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS()** - Checks for pending part switches at frame boundaries
4. **PART_RESOURCE_TABLE** - Maps part IDs to resource pointers

---

### 1. Opcode 0x19 Handler (Part Switch Request)

**File:** `/home/fsanches/devel/custom-kn5000-roms/anotherworld/src/another_world_vm.asm` (lines 2241-2273)

```asm
	; ====  LOAD instruction  ====
	CP A, 19h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_LOAD
	LD WA, (XIX)	; uint16_t resourceId = fetch_word()
	EX W, A			; byte-swap: bytecode is big-endian
	INC 2, XIX

	; resourceId == 0: stop sound (no-op, we don't have sound)
	CP WA, 0
	JP EQ, _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

	; resourceId > 0x91: part switch request
	CP WA, NUM_MEM_LIST		; NUM_MEM_LIST = 0x91 (145)
	JP ULE, _load_check_screen
	LD (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), WA	; Set the part switch request
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

_load_check_screen:
	; Check if resourceId matches a known screen bitmap resource
	; ... (handles screen loading for resourceIds 0x49, 0x53)
```

**Key logic:**
- If `resourceId > 0x91`, it's a part ID
- Sets `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART` to the resource ID
- Otherwise, it loads screen bitmaps (0x49, 0x53)

---

### 2. initForPart() Function

**File:** `/home/fsanches/devel/custom-kn5000-roms/anotherworld/src/another_world_vm.asm` (lines 269-329)

```asm
; initForPart: Reset all threads and prepare for a new game part
; Input: WA = partId
initForPart:
	LD (CURRENT_PART_ID), WA	; Store the part ID

	; Reset VM state
	LD XIX, VM_STACK
	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX

	; Reset all threads: inactive and unfrozen
	LD IX, 0
_initForPart_loop:
	PUSH IX
	SLA 2, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD		; Mark thread as inactive (0xFFFF)
	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST	; Clear requested PC
	POP IX

	PUSH IX
	SLA 1, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN
	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
	POP IX

	INC IX
	CP IX, 64
	JP NE, _initForPart_loop

	; Start thread 0 at PC=0
	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 0

	; Set variable 0xE4 = 0x14 (as per reference)
	LD A, 0E4h
	LD DE, 014h
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; Load resource pointers from PART_RESOURCE_TABLE
	; Table index = (partId - GAME_PART_FIRST) * 16 (4 DDs per entry)
	LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
	SUB WA, GAME_PART_FIRST			; Convert part ID to index (0-9)
	; WA = part index (0-9)
	SLA 4, WA						; WA = index * 16 (4 DDs × 4 bytes each)
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, PART_RESOURCE_TABLE	; XWA points to resource entry

	; XWA now points to: [palette_ptr, bytecode_ptr, video1_ptr, video2_ptr]
	LD XIX, XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 4)	; bytecode pointer (offset 4)
	LD (CUR_BYTECODE), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 8)	; video1 pointer (offset 8)
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_DATA), XWA
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_1), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 12)	; video2 pointer (offset 12)
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_2), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 0)	; palette pointer (offset 0)
	LD (CUR_PALETTES), XWA
	RET
```

**What it does:**
1. **Stores the part ID** in `CURRENT_PART_ID`
2. **Resets all 64 threads** to INACTIVE (0xFFFF) and NOT_FROZEN
3. **Starts thread 0** at PC=0
4. **Sets VM variable 0xE4** to 0x14 (reference behavior)
5. **Loads resource pointers** from `PART_RESOURCE_TABLE`:
   - Palette pointer → `CUR_PALETTES`
   - Bytecode pointer → `CUR_BYTECODE`
   - Video1 pointer → `CUR_VIDEO_DATA` and `CUR_VIDEO_1`
   - Video2 pointer → `CUR_VIDEO_2`

---

### 3. Part Switch Detection (CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS)

**File:** `/home/fsanches/devel/custom-kn5000-roms/anotherworld/src/another_world_vm.asm` (lines 1189-1198)

```asm
CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS:

	; Check if a part switch has been requested
	LD WA, (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART)
	CP WA, 0
	JP EQ, _no_part_switch
	; Part switch requested - call initForPart
	CALL initForPart
	LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0	; Clear the request
_no_part_switch:

	; ... (rest of thread request handling)
```

**When it runs:** Called at the end of each frame (after all threads execute)

---

### 4. Part Resource Table

**File:** `/home/fsanches/devel/custom-kn5000-roms/anotherworld/src/another_world_vm.asm` (lines 2362-2382)

```asm
PART_RESOURCE_TABLE:
	; Part 0: Protection
	dd PART0_PALETTES, PART0_BYTECODE, PART0_VIDEO_1, 0
	; Part 1: Intro
	dd PART1_PALETTES, PART1_BYTECODE, PART1_VIDEO_1, 0
	; Part 2: Water
	dd PART2_PALETTES, PART2_BYTECODE, PART2_VIDEO_1, SHARED_VIDEO_2
	; Part 3: Jail
	dd PART3_PALETTES, PART3_BYTECODE, PART3_VIDEO_1, SHARED_VIDEO_2
	; Part 4: Citadel
	dd PART4_PALETTES, PART4_BYTECODE, PART4_VIDEO_1, SHARED_VIDEO_2
	; Part 5: Battlechar
	dd PART5_PALETTES, PART5_BYTECODE, PART5_VIDEO_1, 0
	; Part 6: Arena
	dd PART6_PALETTES, PART6_BYTECODE, PART6_VIDEO_1, SHARED_VIDEO_2
	; Part 7: Final
	dd PART7_PALETTES, PART7_BYTECODE, PART7_VIDEO_1, SHARED_VIDEO_2
	; Part 8: Password
	dd PART8_PALETTES, PART8_BYTECODE, PART8_VIDEO_1, 0
	; Part 9: Password (same)
	dd PART8_PALETTES, PART8_BYTECODE, PART8_VIDEO_1, 0
```

Each entry is 16 bytes (4 × 32-bit pointers):
- **Offset 0:** Palette pointer
- **Offset 4:** Bytecode pointer
- **Offset 8:** Video1 pointer
- **Offset 12:** Video2 pointer (0 if not used)

---

### 5. Part ID Constants

**File:** `/home/fsanches/devel/custom-kn5000-roms/anotherworld/src/another_world_vm.asm` (lines 66-79)

```asm
GAME_PART_FIRST			EQU 03E80h
GAME_PART_PROTECTION	EQU 03E80h	; Part 0: Copy protection
GAME_PART_INTRO			EQU 03E81h	; Part 1: Introduction cinematic
GAME_PART_WATER			EQU 03E82h	; Part 2: Water / lake
GAME_PART_JAIL			EQU 03E83h	; Part 3: Jail / prison
GAME_PART_CITADEL		EQU 03E84h	; Part 4: Citadel
GAME_PART_BATTLECHAR	EQU 03E85h	; Part 5: Battle cinematic
GAME_PART_ARENA			EQU 03E86h	; Part 6: Arena
GAME_PART_FINAL			EQU 03E87h	; Part 7: Final / ending
GAME_PART_PASSWORD1		EQU 03E88h	; Part 8: Password entry
GAME_PART_PASSWORD2		EQU 03E89h	; Part 9: Password entry (alt)
NUM_MEM_LIST			EQU 091h	; Threshold for part switch (resources > 0x91 = parts)
```

---

### 6. Global Variables

**File:** `/home/fsanches/devel/custom-kn5000-roms/anotherworld/src/main.asm` (lines 107-108)

```asm
REQUESTED_NEXT_PART: DW ?		; Part switch request (0 = no request)
CURRENT_PART_ID: DW ?			; Current game part ID
```

---

## Summary

The part switching system works as follows:

1. **Bytecode triggers a switch** via opcode 0x19 with a resource ID > 0x91
2. **Request is stored** in `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART`
3. **At frame end**, `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS` detects the request
4. **initForPart() is called** with the part ID:
   - Stores the part ID in `CURRENT_PART_ID`
   - Resets all 64 threads (inactive, unfrozen)
   - Resets thread 0 to PC=0
   - Looks up the part index in `PART_RESOURCE_TABLE`
   - Loads the 4 resource pointers (palette, bytecode, video1, video2)
   - Updates the global `CUR_BYTECODE`, `CUR_VIDEO_DATA`, etc.
5. **Next frame execution** uses the new resources

The implementation is complete and functional—all game part transitions (intro→lake→jail, etc.) are supported.

1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→Custom ROM development for the **Technics KN5000** arranger keyboard. ROMs can be tested in MAME's kn5000 driver and potentially installed on real hardware.
     8→
     9→**Target Hardware:**
    10→- CPU: Toshiba TMP94C241F (TLCS-900/H2), 32-bit CISC
    11→  - 16 MHz (2 x 8 MHz XTAL)
    12→- Display: MN89304 VGA-compatible LCD controller, 320x240 @ 8bpp
    13→- Serial: SC0 for MIDI/Computer Interface, SC1 for Control Panel
    14→- Memory: 2MB Program ROM at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF, 512KB VRAM at 0x1A0000
    15→
    16→## Build Commands
    17→
    18→```bash
    19→make          # Build maincpu ROM and create MAME ROM set (default)
    20→make maincpu  # Build as standalone main CPU ROM (2MB, for MAME testing)
    21→make extension# Build as HDAE5000 extension board ROM (512KB)
    22→make build    # Build custom ROM only (out/custom_program.rom)
    23→make romset   # Create complete MAME ROM set
    24→make test     # Run in MAME emulator
    25→make clean    # Remove build artifacts (preserves ROM set)
    26→make distclean# Remove everything including ROM set
    27→make check    # Verify tools and original ROMs are available
    28→```
    29→
    30→**Dual-target build:** Uses `ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU` / `ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION` conditional assembly in `src/main.asm`. The VM code in `src/another_world_vm.asm` is shared between both targets.
    31→
    32→**Requirements:**
    33→- ASL Macro Assembler at `../../tools/asl/asl`
    34→- Original KN5000 ROMs at `/mnt/shared/kn5000_original_roms/kn5000/`
    35→- Game resources in `src/resources/` and `src/` (see README for extraction)
    36→
    37→**Output:**
    38→- Build artifacts: `out/`
    39→- MAME ROM set: `/mnt/shared/custom_kn5000_roms/anotherworld/kn5000/`
    40→
    41→## Architecture
    42→
    43→**Maincpu target** initializes at reset vector 0xFFFEE0, then:
    44→1. Disables watchdog, sets up stack
    45→2. Configures memory controller and DRAM
    46→3. Initializes VGA display (320x240, 8bpp palette mode)
    47→4. Jumps to VM ENTRY point
    48→
    49→**Extension target** is loaded by the KN5000 firmware via the XAPR header and jumps directly to the VM ENTRY point.
    50→
    51→**Memory layout differs by target:**
    52→- **Maincpu:** RAM at 0x010000, page buffers at 0x020000-0x050000, offscreen at 0x060000 (in 1MB DRAM)
    53→- **Extension:** RAM at 0x200000, page buffers at 0x240000-0x270000 (in 512KB extension SRAM)
    54→
    55→**Key source files:**
    56→- `src/main.asm` - Unified platform wrapper (conditional assembly for maincpu/extension)
    57→- `src/another_world_vm.asm` - Another World bytecode VM (shared between targets)
    58→- `src/includes/local_macros.inc` - TLCS-900 instruction macros for ASL
    59→
    60→## Reference Repositories (Read-Only)
    61→
    62→These sibling repositories contain essential reference material. **Do not modify them; all changes go in this repo only.**
    63→
    64→### Hardware Documentation: `../../kn5000-docs/`
    65→| Topic | File | Key Information |
    66→|-------|------|-----------------|
    67→| Memory Map | `memory-map.md` | ROM/RAM addresses, VRAM at 0x1A0000, VGA at 0x170000 |
    68→| Boot Sequence | `boot-sequence.md` | Two-stage boot, reset vector at 0xFFFEE0 |
    69→| Display | `display-subsystem.md` | MN89304 VGA controller, palette setup |
    70→| CPU | `cpu-subsystem.md` | TLCS-900/H2 architecture, SFR addresses |
    71→| Serial | `serial-debugging-journey.md` | SC0/SC1 protocols, baud rates |
    72→| Inter-CPU | `inter-cpu-protocol.md` | Main/Sub CPU communication via 0x120000 latch |
    73→
    74→### Original ROM Disassembly: `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/`
    75→| Component | File | Contains |
    76→|-----------|------|----------|
    77→| Main CPU Program | `maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm` | Full 2MB disassembly, UI/MIDI routines |
    78→| VGA Init | `shared/vga_init.asm` | Original display initialization sequence |
    79→| VGA Constants | `shared/vga_constants.asm` | Register definitions (copied to our vga.inc) |
    80→| SFR Definitions | `shared/sfr_tmp94c241.asm` | CPU register addresses |
    81→| CPU Macros | `tmp94c241.inc` | ASL instruction encoding macros |
    82→| MIDI Serial | `maincpu/midi_serial_routines.asm` | SC0 TX/RX handlers |
    83→| Sub CPU Boot | `subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.asm` | Sub CPU initialization |
    84→| Symbols | `symbols/maincpu_symbols_reference.txt` | 39,125 named addresses |
    85→| AW VM HLE | `mame_driver/src/devices/cpu/anotherworld/` | Reference C++ implementation of all opcodes |
    86→
    87→### MAME HLE Reference
    88→- Full commit: https://github.com/felipesanches/mame/commit/7cbb93bc3ee05f5ffdd083081530ac0daa2dfa84
    89→- Local copy: `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/devices/cpu/anotherworld/`
    90→
    91→### Assembler: `../../tools/asl/`
    92→- `asl` - ASL Macro Assembler 1.42 Beta
    93→- `p2bin` - Converts .p intermediate files to raw binary ROM
    94→
    95→## TLCS-900 Assembly Notes
    96→
    97→**ASL quirks for TMP94C241:**
    98→- Use `cpu 96c141` directive
    99→- Some instructions need macros (see `macros.inc`): `LDIR_94`, `LDA_XWA_IMM24`, `CALR`
   100→- 24-bit addresses require special encoding macros
   101→- Registers: XWA/XBC/XDE/XHL (32-bit), WA/BC/DE/HL (16-bit), A/B/C/D/E/H/L (8-bit)
   102→
   103→**Memory access:**
   104→```asm
   105→ld (addr), value      ; Direct addressing (16-bit addr)
   106→ld (XDE), A           ; Register indirect
   107→LDA_XWA_IMM24 addr    ; Load 24-bit address into XWA
   108→```
   109→
   110→## Hardware Quick Reference
   111→
   112→**VGA Display:**
   113→- Base: 0x170000 (+ VGA port offset, e.g., 0x1703C8 for DAC)
   114→- VRAM: 0x1A0000, linear framebuffer, 1 byte per pixel
   115→- Palette: 6-bit RGB values via DAC registers
   116→
   117→**Serial Port SC0:**
   118→- SC0BUF (0xD0): Data buffer
   119→- SC0CR (0xD1): Control (bit 1 = TX empty)
   120→- SC0MOD (0xD2): Mode (0x29 = 8N1 with baud gen)
   121→- BR0CR (0xD3): Baud rate (0x06 = 38400)
   122→
   123→**Timers (T0/T1 cascade → INTT1 ISR):**
   124→- 12,500 Hz tick rate (80µs/tick) at MAME's 16 MHz clock
   125→- `TICKS_PER_SLICE = 250` (~20ms); PAUSE reads `var[0xFF]` for frame duration
   126→- Prescaler requires `LD (T16RUN), 080h` — T8RUN alone is not enough in MAME
   127→- See [`docs/timer-frame-timing.md`](docs/timer-frame-timing.md) for full details and MAME vs real hardware differences
   128→
   129→**Boot Requirements:**
   130→1. Disable watchdog: `ld (WDMOD), 0` then `ld (WDCR), 0xB1`
   131→2. Configure memory controller (MSAR/MAMR registers)
   132→3. Initialize DRAM with timing delays
   133→4. Set stack pointer to internal RAM
   134→
   135→## Another World VM Architecture
   136→
   137→The VM interprets big-endian bytecode (Amiga/68k origin) on a little-endian TLCS-900 CPU.
   138→
   139→**Bytecode execution:**
   140→- `XIX` register points to current bytecode position during instruction execution
   141→- `_end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION` recomputes `VM_PC` from `XIX` offset — XIX must point to bytecode
   142→- `_after_PC_update` skips VM_PC recomputation — use when VM_PC was already set (JMP, CALL, RET, NEXT_THREAD)
   143→- Opcodes that replace XIX with non-bytecode pointers (0x80, 0x40 video) must save VM_PC BEFORE the replacement and use `_after_PC_update`
   144→
   145→**Thread model:**
   146→- 64 threads, each with a PC slot in `THREADS_DATA` and activation state in `VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE`
   147→- `pauseThread` saves requested_PC; `NEXT_THREAD` scans for next active thread
   148→- `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS` commits requested_PC → PC at frame boundaries
   149→- `INACTIVE_THREAD` (0xFFFE) marks unused thread slots
   150→
   151→**Video pages:**
   152→- 4 page buffers (320x240 @ 8bpp = 76,800 bytes each)
   153→- Page IDs: 0-3 map directly; 0xFF = current back buffer; 0xFE = current front buffer
   154→- `GET_PAGE_PTR` resolves page ID → 24-bit address
   155→
   156→**Endianness:** All `fetch_word()` operations must byte-swap with `EX W, A` after reading via `LD WA, (XIX)`.
   157→
   158→**Helper functions:**
   159→- `_read_vm_var`: Input A=index, Output DE=value (clobbers XIY/XWA)
   160→- `_write_vm_var`: Input A=index, DE=value (clobbers XIY/XWA)
   161→
   162→**Reference implementation:** MAME HLE at `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/devices/cpu/anotherworld/`
   163→
   164→**Resources (intro/part 1):**
   165→- Bytecode: `src/resources/resource-0x18.bin`
   166→- Palettes: `src/resources/resource-0x17.bin` (16 colors/palette, 2 bytes/color, 0x0RGB format)
   167→- Video polygons: `src/resources/resource-0x19.bin` (video1), `resource-0x1a.bin` (video2)
   168→- Screen bitmaps: `src/resources/resource-0x49.bin`, `resource-0x53.bin`
   169→
   170→## TLCS-900 Pitfalls (Learned from Debugging)
   171→
   172→**INC instruction encoding:** Only supports values 1, 2, 4, 8 (encoded in 2-bit field). ASL assembler silently accepts any value but encodes raw bits. MAME treats the 3-bit field literally (`value ? value : 8`), so `INC 3` "works" in MAME but is **undefined on real TMP94C241F**. Always use `ADD` for non-power-of-2 increments.
   173→
   174→**Register clobbering:**
   175→- `LD BC, WA` clobbers B — save B to stack first if needed later
   176→- `POP WA` restores both W and A — don't follow with `LD A, W` (overwrites restored A)
   177→- `LDIRW` uses XHL=src, XDE=dst, XBC=word_count (not XIX/XIY)
   178→
   179→**Signed vs unsigned shifts:** `SRA` (arithmetic shift right) sign-extends; `SRL` (logical shift right) zero-fills. Use `SRL` for unsigned nibble extraction (e.g., extracting high nibble of a byte).
   180→
   181→**MAME TLCS-900 bugs:**
   182→- `DEC 1, rr; JP NZ` doesn't work — DEC doesn't set flags correctly. Use `DJNZ rr, label` instead.
   183→- Prescaler requires T16RUN bit 7 (not just T8RUN). See [`docs/timer-frame-timing.md`](docs/timer-frame-timing.md).
   184→- MAME's T01MOD register layout and prescaler divisions differ from the TMP94C241F datasheet.
   185→
   186→**AW palette → VGA DAC conversion:**
   187→- AW format: 2 bytes/color, `0x0RGB`. Byte 0 low nibble = R, byte 1 high nibble = G, byte 1 low nibble = B
   188→- VGA DAC expects 6-bit values (0-63) in R, G, B order; AW uses 4-bit (0-15)
   189→- Must `SLA 2, A` to scale each channel from 4-bit to 6-bit
   190→
   191→## Mandatory Policy: Conversation Logs
   192→
   193→**Every Claude Code session that makes changes to this project MUST save its full conversation transcript before committing.** This is a mandatory policy for this project.
   194→
   195→Procedure:
   196→1. At the end of each session (before or alongside the commit), copy the current conversation JSONL file from `~/.claude/projects/-home-fsanches-devel-custom-kn5000-roms/` to `logs/`
   197→2. Name the log file: `YYYY-MM-DD_short-description.jsonl`
   198→3. If there was a separate planning session, save that too with a `_planning` suffix
   199→4. Include the log files in the commit
   200→
   201→Log directory: `logs/`
   202→
   203→## Expanding This ROM
   204→
   205→To add new features, study the corresponding routines in the disassembly:
   206→- **Keyboard scanning:** `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/cpanel_routines.asm`
   207→- **Floppy disk:** `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/fdc_routines.asm`
   208→- **Sound generation:** Requires Sub CPU payload via inter-CPU protocol
   209→- **MIDI:** `../../kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/midi_serial_routines.asm`

1→; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>
     2→; Licensed under GPL version 2 or later.
     3→;
     4→; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
     5→; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
     6→; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
     7→;
     8→; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
     9→;
    10→; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
    11→; as a high-level emulation on MAME
    12→;
    13→; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
    14→; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
    15→;
    16→; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
    17→; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
    18→;
    19→; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
    20→; using the scripts provided at:
    21→; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
    22→;
    23→; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
    24→PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
    25→REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
    26→INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
    27→DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
    28→NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh
    29→TICKS_PER_SLICE		EQU 250		; ~20ms at 12500 Hz tick rate (80 µs/tick)
    30→
    31→CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
    32→REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte
    33→
    34→FROZEN	EQU 0
    35→NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
    36→NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh
    37→
    38→; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
    39→; MAINCPU: in DRAM at 0x020000-0x05FFFF
    40→; EXTENSION: in extension board SRAM at 0x240000-0x27FFFF
    41→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
    42→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 020000h
    43→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 030000h
    44→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 040000h
    45→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 050000h
    46→	endif
    47→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
    48→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
    49→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
    50→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
    51→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h
    52→	endif
    53→
    54→; VM variable indices (used by the game engine)
    55→VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED		EQU 03Ch
    56→VM_VARIABLE_LAST_KEYCHAR	EQU 0C5h
    57→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN	EQU 0E5h
    58→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN	EQU 0DCh
    59→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT	EQU 0E9h
    60→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK	EQU 0FAh
    61→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION		EQU 0FBh
    62→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK EQU 0FBh
    63→VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y		EQU 0F9h
    64→
    65→; Game part IDs (from reference: parts.h)
    66→GAME_PART_FIRST			EQU 03E80h

## Summary

Based on my search of the MAME HLE reference and the custom KN5000 Another World VM implementation, here are the answers to your three questions:

### 1. What happens when opcode 0x19 gets a resourceId > NUM_MEM_LIST

**File:** `/home/fsanches/devel/custom-kn5000-roms/anotherworld/src/another_world_vm.asm`, lines 2241-2255

```asm
; ====  LOAD instruction (opcode 0x19) ====
CP A, 19h
JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_LOAD
LD WA, (XIX)	; uint16_t resourceId = fetch_word()
EX W, A			; byte-swap: bytecode is big-endian
INC 2, XIX

; resourceId == 0: stop sound (no-op, we don't have sound)
CP WA, 0
JP EQ, _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

; resourceId > 0x91: part switch request
CP WA, NUM_MEM_LIST
JP ULE, _load_check_screen
LD (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), WA
JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
```

**What happens:** When `resourceId > NUM_MEM_LIST` (0x91), it's treated as a **game part switch request**. The resourceId is written to `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART` register and the instruction completes. The actual part switch happens at the next frame boundary during `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS`.

**Constants:**
- `NUM_MEM_LIST = 0x91` (defined at line 79)
- Part IDs range from 0x3E80 (GAME_PART_PROTECTION) to 0x3E89 (GAME_PART_PASSWORD2)

---

### 2. How changeGamePart works

There is no function literally called `changeGamePart` in the custom implementation. Instead, the mechanism is:

**Part switching flow (lines 1192-1197):**
```asm
LD WA, (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART)
CP WA, 0
JP EQ, _no_part_switch
; Part switch requested - call initForPart
CALL initForPart
LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
_no_part_switch:
```

**The actual switching function is `initForPart` (lines 271-329):**

```asm
initForPart:
	LD (CURRENT_PART_ID), WA
	
	; Reset VM state
	LD XIX, VM_STACK
	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX
	
	; Reset all threads: inactive and unfrozen (loops through 64 threads)
	LD IX, 0
_initForPart_loop:
	PUSH IX
	SLA 2, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
	POP IX
	
	PUSH IX
	SLA 1, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN
	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
	POP IX
	
	INC IX
	CP IX, 64
	JP NE, _initForPart_loop
	
	; Start thread 0 at PC=0
	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 0
	
	; Set variable 0xE4 = 0x14 (as per reference)
	LD A, 0E4h
	LD DE, 014h
	CALL _write_vm_var
	
	; Load resource pointers from PART_RESOURCE_TABLE
	; Table index = (partId - GAME_PART_FIRST) * 16 (4 DDs per entry)
	LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
	SUB WA, GAME_PART_FIRST
	; WA = part index (0-9)
	SLA 4, WA			; WA = index * 16
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, PART_RESOURCE_TABLE
	
	; XWA now points to: [palette_ptr, bytecode_ptr, video1_ptr, video2_ptr]
	LD XIX, XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 4)	; bytecode pointer
	LD (CUR_BYTECODE), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 8)	; video1 pointer
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_DATA), XWA
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_1), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 12)	; video2 pointer
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_2), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 0)	; palette pointer
	LD (CUR_PALETTES), XWA
	RET
```

**What it does:**
1. Stores the new part ID in `CURRENT_PART_ID`
2. Resets the VM stack pointer
3. Marks all 64 threads as inactive and unfrozen
4. Sets thread 0 PC to 0 (start of bytecode)
5. Sets variable 0xE4 to 0x14
6. Looks up the part's resource table entry: `PART_RESOURCE_TABLE + (partId - 0x3E80) * 16`
7. Loads 4 resource pointers: palette, bytecode, video1, video2

The PART_RESOURCE_TABLE (lines 2362-2382) stores 10 entries (one per part):
```asm
PART_RESOURCE_TABLE:
	dd PART0_PALETTES, PART0_BYTECODE, PART0_VIDEO_1, 0
	dd PART1_PALETTES, PART1_BYTECODE, PART1_VIDEO_1, 0
	dd PART2_PALETTES, PART2_BYTECODE, PART2_VIDEO_1, SHARED_VIDEO_2
	...
	dd PART8_PALETTES, PART8_BYTECODE, PART8_VIDEO_1, 0
	dd PART8_PALETTES, PART8_BYTECODE, PART8_VIDEO_1, 0  ; Part 9 reuses Part 8
```

---

### 3. What the VM_HACK for var 0xDC does exactly

**Full implementation (lines 2047-2061):**

```asm
; VM_HACK_SWITCH_FROM_INTRO_TO_LAKE:
; If currentPart == INTRO and vm_var[0x67] == 1, set vm_var[0xDC] = 0x21
PUSH WA			; save pageId
LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
CP WA, GAME_PART_INTRO
JP NE, _blit_no_hack
LD A, 067h
CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vm_var[0x67]
CP DE, 1
JP NE, _blit_no_hack
LD A, 0DCh
LD DE, 021h
CALL _write_vm_var
_blit_no_hack:
POP WA			; restore pageId (A = pageId)
CALL UPDATE_DISPLAY
CALL PAUSE			; Frame timing delay
```

**What it does:**
- This hack is executed during the **BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER instruction (opcode 0x10)** on every frame
- **Condition:** Only applies when:
  - Current part is INTRO (`GAME_PART_INTRO = 0x3E81`)
  - AND variable 0x67 equals 1
- **Action:** Sets `vm_var[0xDC] = 0x21`
- **Variable 0xDC:** `VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN` (line 58) - controls the hero's jump-down position

**Purpose:** This is a **workaround to transition from the intro cinematic to the Lake/Water part**. The intro bytecode sets vm_var[0x67] to signal completion, and the hack automatically updates the hero's jump position variable to prepare for the water part sequence.

; initForPart: Reset all threads and prepare for a new game part
; Input: WA = partId
initForPart:
	LD (CURRENT_PART_ID), WA

	; Reset VM state
	LD XIX, VM_STACK
	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX

	PUSH IX
	SLA 2, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST

	SLA 1, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN
	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
	POP IX

	INC IX
	CP IX, 64
	JP NE, _initForPart_loop

	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 0

	; Load resource pointers from PART_RESOURCE_TABLE
	; Table index = (partId - GAME_PART_FIRST) * 16 (4 DDs per entry)
	LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
	SUB WA, GAME_PART_FIRST
	; WA = part index (0-9)
	SLA 4, WA			; WA = index * 16
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, PART_RESOURCE_TABLE

	; XWA now points to: [palette_ptr, bytecode_ptr, video1_ptr, video2_ptr]
	LD XIX, XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 4)	; bytecode pointer
	LD (CUR_BYTECODE), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 8)	; video1 pointer
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_DATA), XWA
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_1), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 12)	; video2 pointer
	LD (CUR_VIDEO_2), XWA
	LD XWA, (XIX + 0)	; palette pointer
	LD (CUR_PALETTES), XWA
	RET
