    11→;     CPanel_SendInitSequence   - Send initialization sequence to panels
    12→;     CPanel_InitLEDBuffer      - Initialize LED TX buffer
    13→;     CPanel_InitButtonState    - Initialize button state arrays
    14→;
    15→;   Button Handling:
    16→;     CPanel_ScanButtons        - Main button scan entry point
    17→;     CPanel_ReadAllButtons     - Read button states from both panels
    18→;     CPanel_CheckSpecialCombos - Check for special button combinations
    19→;     CPanel_PollStartup        - Poll buttons during startup
    20→;     CPanel_ButtonPollLoop     - Button polling loop
    21→;     CPanel_EncoderCheck       - Check encoder state
    22→;
    23→;   Serial Communication:
    24→;     CPanel_WaitTXReady        - Wait for TX ready
    25→;     CPanel_SendCommand        - Send command to panel
    26→;
    27→;   State Machine:
    28→;     CPANEL_STATE_MACHINE_TABLE - State machine jump table
    29→;     CPanel_SM_StartTX         - Start TX state
    30→;     CPanel_SM_TXDelay1/2      - TX delay states
    31→;     CPanel_SM_SendByte1/N     - Send byte states
    32→;     CPanel_SM_TXComplete      - TX complete state
    33→;     CPanel_SM_RXByte1/N       - Receive byte states
    34→;     CPanel_SM_Idle            - Idle state
    35→;
    36→;   Packet Processing:
    37→;     CPanel_RX_ProcessWithFlag - Process RX with flag
    38→;     CPanel_RX_Process         - Main RX processing
    39→;     CPanel_RX_ParseNext       - Parse next packet
    40→;     CPanel_RX_PacketHandlers  - Packet type dispatch table
    41→;     CPanel_RX_ButtonPacket    - Handle button packets
    42→;     CPanel_RX_EncoderPacket   - Handle encoder packets
    43→;     CPanel_RX_MultiBytePacket - Handle multi-byte packets
    44→;     CPanel_RX_SyncPacket      - Handle sync packets
    45→;
    46→;   LED Control:
    47→;     CPanel_UpdateLEDs         - Update LED states
    48→;     CPanel_LED_PacketHandlers - LED packet dispatch table
    49→;
    50→;   Buffer Management:
    51→;     CPanel_IncRXPtr           - Increment RX buffer pointer
    52→;     CPanel_IncLEDPtr          - Increment LED buffer pointer
    53→;     CPanel_IncEventPtr        - Increment event queue pointer
    54→;     CPanel_DecEventPtr        - Decrement event queue pointer
    55→;
    56→; Required includes before this file:
    57→;   - cpanel_constants.asm (or equivalent EQU definitions)
    58→;
    59→; =============================================================================
    60→
    61→CPanel_ScanButtons:		; FC3EE5
    62→	PUSH XIX
    63→	PUSH XIZ
    64→	PUSH XHL
    65→	PUSH XDE
    66→	CALL CPanel_ReadAllButtons
    67→	POP XDE
    68→	POP XHL
    69→	POP XIZ
    70→	POP XIX
    71→	CALR CPanel_CheckSpecialCombos
    72→	RET
    73→
    74→
    75→CPanel_InitHardware:
    76→	LD XHL, CPANEL_RX_EVENT_QUEUE
    77→	LDW (XHL - 4), 0000h
    78→	LDW (XHL - 8), 0000h
    79→	LDW (XHL - 2), 0080h
    80→
    81→	LD XHL, CPANEL_LED_EVENT_QUEUE
    82→	LDW (XHL - 4), 0000h
    83→	LDW (XHL - 8), 0000h
    84→	LDW (XHL - 2), 0080h
    85→
    86→	LD_A 003h ; PF2=SCK0 Disabled, PF0=TxD0 and PF1=RXD0 (MIDI)
    87→	AND A, 0afh ; PF6=SCK1 Disabled, PF4=TxD1 and PF5=RXD1 (Control Panel)
    88→	LD (PFFC_VALUE), A
    89→	LD (PFFC), A
    90→	LD_A 015h
    91→	AND A, 08fh
    92→	LD (PFCR_VALUE), A
    93→	LD (PFCR), A
    94→	AND (PF), 0bfh ; PF bit 6, (SCLK1 | /CTS1) = 0
    95→	LD_A 000h
    96→	LD (PEFC), A
    97→	LD_A 046h
    98→	LD (PECR), A
    99→	LD (SC1MOD), 000h ; serial clk: TO2 trigger
   100→	                  ; serial transfer mode: I/O  transfer mode

1→; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>
     2→; Licensed under GPL version 2 or later.
     3→;
     4→; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
     5→; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
     6→; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
     7→;
     8→; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
     9→;
    10→; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
    11→; as a high-level emulation on MAME
    12→;
    13→; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
    14→; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
    15→;
    16→; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
    17→; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
    18→;
    19→; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
    20→; using the scripts provided at:
    21→; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
    22→;
    23→; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
    24→PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
    25→REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
    26→INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
    27→DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
    28→NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh
    29→TICKS_PER_SLICE		EQU 250		; ~20ms at 12500 Hz tick rate (80 µs/tick)
    30→
    31→CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
    32→REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte
    33→
    34→FROZEN	EQU 0
    35→NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
    36→NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh
    37→
    38→; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
    39→; MAINCPU: in DRAM at 0x020000-0x05FFFF
    40→; EXTENSION: in extension board SRAM at 0x240000-0x27FFFF
    41→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
    42→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 020000h
    43→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 030000h
    44→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 040000h
    45→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 050000h
    46→	endif
    47→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
    48→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
    49→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
    50→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
    51→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h
    52→	endif
    53→
    54→; VM variable indices (used by the game engine)
    55→VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED		EQU 03Ch
    56→VM_VARIABLE_LAST_KEYCHAR	EQU 0C5h
    57→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN	EQU 0E5h
    58→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN	EQU 0DCh
    59→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT	EQU 0E9h
    60→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK	EQU 0FAh
    61→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION		EQU 0FBh
    62→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK EQU 0FBh
    63→VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y		EQU 0F9h
    64→
    65→; Game part IDs (from reference: parts.h)
    66→GAME_PART_FIRST			EQU 03E80h
    67→GAME_PART_PROTECTION	EQU 03E80h	; Part 0: Copy protection
    68→GAME_PART_INTRO			EQU 03E81h	; Part 1: Introduction cinematic
    69→GAME_PART_WATER			EQU 03E82h	; Part 2: Water / lake
    70→GAME_PART_JAIL			EQU 03E83h	; Part 3: Jail / prison
    71→GAME_PART_CITADEL		EQU 03E84h	; Part 4: Citadel
    72→GAME_PART_BATTLECHAR	EQU 03E85h	; Part 5: Battle cinematic
    73→GAME_PART_ARENA			EQU 03E86h	; Part 6: Arena
    74→GAME_PART_FINAL			EQU 03E87h	; Part 7: Final / ending
    75→GAME_PART_PASSWORD1		EQU 03E88h	; Part 8: Password entry
    76→GAME_PART_PASSWORD2		EQU 03E89h	; Part 9: Password entry (alt)
    77→GAME_PART_LAST			EQU 03E89h
    78→GAME_NUM_PARTS			EQU 10
    79→NUM_MEM_LIST			EQU 091h
    80→
    81→CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN:
    82→	; int16_t xmax = MAX(x1, x2);
    83→	LD WA, (X1)
    84→	CP WA, (X2)
    85→	JP GT, XMAX_OK
    86→	LD WA, (X2)
    87→XMAX_OK:
    88→	LD (LINE_XMAX), WA
    89→	
    90→	; int16_t xmin = MIN(x1, x2);
    91→	LD WA, (X1)
    92→	CP WA, (X2)
    93→	JP LT, XMIN_OK
    94→	LD WA, (X2)
    95→XMIN_OK:
    96→	LD (LINE_XMIN), WA
    97→	RET
    98→
    99→drawLineN:
   100→	; Inputs:
   101→	; C = color
   102→	PUSH XIX
   103→	PUSH XHL
   104→	
   105→	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN
   106→
   107→	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
   108→	; 	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = color;
   109→	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
   110→	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   111→	EXTS XHL
   112→	ADD XIX, XHL
   113→	LD HL, (LINE_XMAX)
   114→	SUB HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   115→	INC HL				; inclusive range: xmax-xmin+1 pixels
   116→
   117→drawLineN_loop:
   118→	LDB (XIX), C
   119→	INC XIX
   120→	DJNZ HL, drawLineN_loop
   121→	
   122→	POP XHL
   123→	POP XIX
   124→	RET
   125→
   126→drawLineP:
   127→	; Copy pixels from PAGE_BITMAP_0 to curPagePtr1
   128→	PUSH XIX
   129→	PUSH XIY
   130→	PUSH XHL
   131→
   132→	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN
   133→
   134→	; Destination: CUR_LINE + LINE_XMIN (in curPagePtr1)
   135→	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
   136→	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   137→	EXTS XHL
   138→	ADD XIX, XHL
   139→
   140→	; Source: PAGE_BITMAP_0 + HLINEY*320 + LINE_XMIN
   141→	LD XIY, PAGE_BITMAP_0
   142→	LD XWA, 0
   143→	LD WA, (HLINEY)
   144→	LD DE, 320
   145→	MUL XWA, DE
   146→	ADD XIY, XWA
   147→	LD XHL, 0
   148→	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
   149→	EXTS XHL
   150→	ADD XIY, XHL

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

## MAME Input Ports (from kn5000.cpp)
The MAME driver has keyboard-mapped buttons. Relevant navigation buttons from the LEFT panel:

CPL_SEG7 (8 bits): RIGHT 4, RIGHT 5, DISPLAY_HOLD, EXIT, UP 7, DOWN 7, UP 8, DOWN 8
CPL_SEG8 (8 bits): RIGHT 1, RIGHT 2, RIGHT 3, (unused), UP 5, DOWN 5, UP 6, DOWN 6  
CPL_SEG9 (8 bits): LEFT 3, LEFT 4, LEFT 5, (unused), UP 3, DOWN 3, UP 4, DOWN 4
CPL_SEG10 (8 bits): LEFT 1, LEFT 2, HELP, OTHER_PARTS, UP 1, DOWN 1, UP 2, DOWN 2

These would need keyboard key bindings in MAME (arrow keys, space, etc.).

## Existing Code Structure
- `src/another_world_vm.asm`: VM implementation, ~2400 lines
- `src/main.asm`: Platform setup, RAM variables, timer ISR
- VM frame loop: MAIN_LOOP → EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION → ... → NEXT_THREAD → (back to MAIN_LOOP)
- `_write_vm_var`: Input A=index, DE=value
- PAUSE function polls SYSTEM_TICKS for frame timing
- NEXT_THREAD processes thread switching + part switching at frame boundaries

## Files to read for exact register addresses and protocol:
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.asm` for SFR addresses
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` for full protocol
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` and `.cpp` for what the MAME HLE expects
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/cpanel_routines.asm` for existing firmware button polling

## Design Requirements
1. Read control panel button state each frame
2. Map specific buttons to: Left, Right, Up, Down, Action
3. Update VM variables: 0xE5, 0xFA, 0xFB, 0xFC, 0xFD, 0xFE
4. Call input update from the VM frame loop (NEXT_THREAD area or PAUSE)
5. Must work in MAME testing; real hardware is a bonus

Please design a detailed implementation plan. Consider:
- How to initialize SC1 for cpanel communication
- How to poll buttons (blocking vs non-blocking, timing)

     7→# Control Panel Serial Protocol - MAME HLE Implementation Guide
     8→
     9→This document provides comprehensive information for implementing High Level Emulation (HLE) of the KN5000 control panel MCUs in MAME.
    10→
    11→## 1. Overview
    12→
    13→### Purpose of Control Panel MCUs
    14→
    15→The KN5000 control panel uses two dedicated Mitsubishi M37471M2196S microcontrollers to handle:
    16→
    17→- **Button scanning** - Matrix scanning of all front panel buttons
    18→- **LED control** - Multiplexed driving of status LEDs
    19→- **Rotary encoders** - Data wheel, pitch bend, and modulation wheels
    20→- **Analog inputs** - Volume sliders and continuous controllers
    21→
    22→### Why HLE is Needed
    23→
    24→The control panel MCUs use **mask ROM** (M2196S suffix indicates a specific mask pattern). Without physical decapping and ROM extraction, the firmware is unavailable. However, the main CPU firmware extensively documents the communication protocol, making HLE feasible.
    25→
    26→**HLE Strategy:**
    27→1. Intercept serial commands from the main CPU
    28→2. Maintain virtual button/LED/encoder state
    29→3. Generate appropriate response packets
    30→4. Interface with MAME input system for user interaction
    31→
    32→## 2. Hardware Architecture
    33→
    34→### MCU Identification
    35→
    36→| Parameter | Value |
    37→|-----------|-------|
    38→| **Part Number** | Mitsubishi M37471M2196S |
    39→| **Architecture** | 8-bit CMOS (Mitsubishi 740 series) |
    40→| **Features** | Built-in A/D, Serial UART, 16 segment outputs |
    41→| **Quantity** | 2 (CPL = Left panel, CPR = Right panel) |
    42→
    43→### Physical Connections
    44→
    45→```
    46→Main CPU (TMP94C241F)                Control Panel MCUs
    47→    Port F, SC1                    +---------+  +---------+
    48→        |                          |   CPL   |  |   CPR   |
    49→        |<----- SOUT --------------|   SOUT--|  |--SOUT   |
    50→        |                          |         |  |         |
    51→        |------ SIN -------------->|   SIN---|  |---SIN   |
    52→        |                          |         |  |         |
    53→        |------ SCLK1 ------------>|   CLK---|  |---CLK   |
    54→        |                          |         |  |         |
    55→        |------ CNTR1 ------------>|  CNTR1--|  |--CNTR1  |
    56→        |                          +---------+  +---------+
    57→        |
    58→   PF.5 (INTA) <---- Interrupt from panels
    59→   PF.6 (SCLK1) ---> Serial clock output / clock detect input
    60→```
    61→
    62→### Serial Interface Specifications
    63→
    64→| Parameter | Value | Notes |
    65→|-----------|-------|-------|
    66→| **Serial Channel** | SC1 (Serial Channel 1) | TMP94C241F UART |
    67→| **Clock Source** | Internal, derived from fc=16MHz | |
    68→| **TX Baud Rate** | 250 kHz | fc/16/4 (BR1CR=0x14) during data TX |
    69→| **Initial Baud Rate** | 31.25 kHz | fc/64/8 (BR1CR=0x28) during init |
    70→| **Data Format** | 8-bit, odd parity (disabled), async | SC1MOD, SC1CR config |
    71→| **Flow Control** | Software (CNTR1 pin for chip select) | |
    72→
    73→### Clock Configuration (from BR1CR register)
    74→
    75→| BR1CR Value | Prescaler | Divider | Baud Rate | Usage |
    76→|-------------|-----------|---------|-----------|-------|
    77→| `0x14` | T2 (fc/16) | /4 | 250 kHz | Normal data transfer |
    78→| `0x24` | T8 (fc/64) | /4 | 62.5 kHz | Idle/reset state |
    79→| `0x28` | T8 (fc/64) | /8 | 31.25 kHz | Initialization |
    80→
    81→## 3. Protocol Specification
    82→
    83→### Command Format
    84→
    85→All commands are **2-byte sequences** sent from main CPU to control panel MCUs:
    86→
    87→```
    88→Byte 0: Command/Address byte
    89→Byte 1: Data/Parameter byte
    90→```
    91→
    92→The high 3 bits of the command byte (bits 7-5) select the target panel:
    93→
    94→| Bits 7-5 | Binary | Target |
    95→|----------|--------|--------|
    96→| 0-3 | `000`-`011` | Left panel (CPL) |
    97→| 4-7 | `100`-`111` | Right panel (CPR) |
    98→
    99→### Complete Command Reference
   100→
   101→#### Initialization Commands
   102→
   103→| Command | Bytes | Purpose | Timing |
   104→|---------|-------|---------|--------|
   105→| `1F DA` | Init sequence 1 | Reset/sync left panel | 3000 loops wait |
   106→| `1F 1A` | Init sequence 2 | Configure left panel | 3000 loops wait |
   107→| `1D 00` | Init sequence 3 | Initialize left panel | 6000 loops wait |
   108→| `DD 03` | Setup mode | Configure both panels | 6000 loops wait |
   109→| `1E 80` | Init sequence 4 | Final init (left) | 9000 loops wait |
   110→
   111→#### Query Commands
   112→
   113→| Command | Bytes | Purpose | Expected Response |
   114→|---------|-------|---------|-------------------|
   115→| `20 00` | Ping left panel | Communication test | Any response = OK |
   116→| `20 0B` | Poll left buttons | Read button segment 0x0B | Button state packet |
   117→| `20 10` | Query left panel | Read status/sync | Sync packet |
   118→| `E0 00` | Ping right panel | Communication test | Any response = OK |
   119→| `E2 04` | Query right panel | Read specific register | Data packet |
   120→| `E2 11` | Query right panel | Read specific register | Data packet |
   121→| `E3 10` | Query right extended | Extended read | Multi-byte packet |
   122→
   123→#### Data Commands
   124→
   125→| Command | Bytes | Purpose |
   126→|---------|-------|---------|
   127→| `25 01` | Left panel data | Set/request data mode |
   128→| `2B 00` | Init state array (left) | Initialize button state |
   129→| `EB 00` | Init state array (right) | Initialize button state |
   130→
   131→### Response Packet Format
   132→
   133→Responses from control panel MCUs are processed by `CPanel_RX_ParseNext` at address `0xFC491A`.
   134→
   135→#### Packet Type Encoding
   136→
   137→The packet type is encoded in bits 5-3 of the first response byte:
   138→
   139→```
   140→Byte 0: [ X | X | Type2 | Type1 | Type0 | X | X | X ]
   141→                 \___________|__________/
   142→                    Packet type (0-7)
   143→```
   144→
   145→#### Packet Type Handlers
   146→
   147→| Type | Bits 5-3 | Handler | Address | Purpose |
   148→|------|----------|---------|---------|---------|
   149→| 0 | `000` | `CPanel_RX_ButtonPacket` | 0xFC4985 | Button state (left panel) |
   150→| 1 | `001` | `CPanel_RX_ButtonPacket` | 0xFC4985 | Button state (right panel) |
   151→| 2 | `010` | `CPanel_RX_EncoderPacket` | 0xFC49E0 | Rotary encoder delta |
   152→| 3 | `011` | `CPanel_RX_SyncPacket` | 0xFC4B10 | Sync/ACK |
   153→| 4 | `100` | `CPanel_RX_SyncPacket` | 0xFC4B10 | Sync/ACK |
   154→| 5 | `101` | `CPanel_RX_SyncPacket` | 0xFC4B10 | Sync/ACK |
   155→| 6 | `110` | `CPanel_RX_MultiBytePacket` | 0xFC4A40 | Multi-byte data |
   156→| 7 | `111` | `CPanel_RX_MultiBytePacket` | 0xFC4A40 | Multi-byte data |
   157→
   158→### Button State Packet Format (Types 0, 1)
   159→
   160→```
   161→Byte 0: [ Panel | Type | Segment Index (bits 3-0 + bit 6) ]
   162→Byte 1: [ Button bitmap - 8 buttons per segment ]
   163→```
   164→
   165→**Segment index calculation:**
   166→- If bit 6 is set: `segment = (byte0 & 0x0F) + 0x10` (left panel offset)
   167→- Otherwise: `segment = byte0 & 0x0F`
   168→
   169→The handler at `CPanel_RX_ButtonPacket`:
   170→1. Extracts segment index: `W = byte0 & 0x4F`
   171→2. Calculates button array offset
   172→3. XORs new state with previous to detect changes
   173→4. Stores result in `CPANEL_LAST_EVENT_VALUE` for edge detection
   174→
   175→### Encoder Packet Format (Type 2)
   176→
   177→```
   178→Byte 0: [ ID_hi[1:0] | 0 | 1 | 0 | ID_lo[2:0] ]
   179→         bits 7-6     5   4   3   bits 2-0
   180→
   181→Byte 1: [ Delta value (signed 8-bit) ]
   182→```
   183→
   184→**Encoder ID Encoding:**
   185→- Bits 0-2 of byte 0 → bits 0-2 of encoder ID
   186→- Bits 6-7 of byte 0 → bits 3-4 of encoder ID
   187→- This gives a 5-bit encoder ID (0-31)
   188→
   189→The encoder dispatch routine `CPanel_EncoderDispatch` (0xFC6C5F):
   190→1. Extracts encoder ID: `ID = (byte0 & 0x07) | ((byte0 >> 3) & 0x18)`
   191→2. Multiplies by 4 for jump table offset
   192→3. Indexes into jump table at `ENCODER_HANDLER_TABLE` (0xEDA0BC)
   193→4. Dispatches to encoder-specific handler
   194→5. Returns 0xFFFF if invalid/no change
   195→
   196→**Known Encoder IDs:**
   197→
   198→| ID | Handler | Output Variable | Physical Control |
   199→|----|---------|-----------------|------------------|
   200→| 2 | `Encoder_ProcessModwheel` | `MIDI_CC_MODWHEEL_VALUE` | Modulation wheel |
   201→| 5 | `Encoder_ProcessVolume` | `MIDI_CC_VOLUME_VALUE` | Volume slider |
   202→| 25 | `Encoder_ProcessBreath` | `MIDI_CC_BREATH_VALUE` | Breath controller |
   203→| 26 | `Encoder_ProcessFoot` | `MIDI_CC_FOOT_VALUE` | Foot controller |
   204→| 27 | `Encoder_ProcessExpression` | `MIDI_CC_EXPRESSION_VALUE` | Expression pedal |
   205→| 31 | `Encoder_ReturnValue` | Direct passthrough | Raw value output |
   206→| 0-1,3-4,6-24,28-30 | `Encoder_ReturnOne` | Returns 1 | Unused |
   207→
   208→**Encoder Processing:**
   209→- Raw input values are inverted (`CPL A`) and stored in `ENCODER_RAW_*` variables
   210→- Values are divided by 2 (`SRL 1, A`) and used as lookup table indices
   211→- Lookup tables at `ENCODER_LUT_*` convert raw values to MIDI CC range (0-127)
   212→- Change detection compares with previous value before storing
   213→
   214→### Timing Requirements
   215→
   216→| Operation | Delay | Method |
   217→|-----------|-------|--------|
   218→| Post-command wait | 6 system ticks | `DELAY_6_TICKS` (0xFC4213) |
   219→| Init command wait | 3000 loop iterations | `DELAY_3000_LOOPS` (0xFC4118) |
   220→| Ready check timeout | 200 attempts * 1500 loops | `CPanel_WaitTXReady` |
   221→
   222→## 4. State Machine
   223→
   224→### Serial Routine State Machine
   225→
   226→The main CPU uses a state machine indexed by `CPANEL_STATE_MACHINE_INDEX` (address 0x8D8A) with values 0-10 (stored as byte offsets 0x00-0x28).
   227→
   228→```
   229→State Transition Diagram:
   230→
   231→    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   232→    │                                                                 │
   233→    │  IDLE (0)                                                       │
   234→    │    │                                                            │
   235→    │    │ CPanel_SendCommand called                                  │
   236→    │    ▼                                                            │
   237→    │  ROUTINE_1 (1) ──► Start TX, check SCLK1                        │
   238→    │    │                │                                           │
   239→    │    │ SCLK1=1        │ SCLK1=0 (panel talking)                   │
   240→    │    ▼                ▼                                           │
   241→    │  ROUTINE_2 (2)    Back to IDLE (0)                              │
   242→    │    │                                                            │
   243→    │    │ TX byte, update LED index                                  │
   244→    │    ▼                                                            │
   245→    │  ROUTINE_3 (3) ──► Disable serial pins                          │
   246→    │    │                                                            │
   247→    │    ▼                                                            │
   248→    │  ROUTINE_4 (4) ──► Continue TX, count down STATE_0_TO_17        │
   249→    │    │                │                                           │
   250→    │    │ count > 1      │ count <= 1                                │
   251→    │    ▼                ▼                                           │
   252→    │  ROUTINE_3 (loop)  ROUTINE_5 (5)                                │
   253→    │                      │                                          │
   254→    │                      ▼                                          │
   255→    │                    ROUTINE_6 (6) ──► Check if more LED data     │
   256→    │                      │       │                                  │
   257→    │                      │ more  │ done                             │
   258→    │                      ▼       ▼                                  │
   259→    │                    ROUTINE_1  IDLE (0)                          │
   260→    │                                                                 │
   261→    │  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════    │
   262→    │                                                                 │
   263→    │  ROUTINE_7 (8) ──► RX phase 1, first byte from panel            │
   264→    │    │                                                            │
   265→    │    │ Byte received, calculate STATE_0_TO_17                     │
   266→    │    ▼                                                            │
   267→    │  ROUTINE_8 (9) ──► RX phase 2, additional bytes                 │
   268→    │    │                │                                           │
   269→    │    │ count > 1      │ count <= 1                                │
   270→    │    ▼                ▼                                           │
   271→    │  ROUTINE_8 (loop)  IDLE (0)                                     │
   272→    │                                                                 │
   273→    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   274→```
   275→
   276→### STATE_0_TO_17 Meaning
   277→
   278→The variable `CPANEL_PACKET_BYTE_COUNT` (address 0x8D8B) tracks the expected byte count in multi-byte transfers:
   279→
   280→| Value | Meaning |
   281→|-------|---------|
   282→| 0 | Idle/complete |
   283→| 1 | Last byte expected |
   284→| 2 | Standard 2-byte packet |
   285→| 3-17 | Extended packet, N bytes remaining |
   286→
   287→**Calculation (from received byte A):**
   288→```c
   289→if ((A & 0x3F) < 0x30) {
   290→    STATE_0_TO_17 = 2;
   291→} else {
   292→    STATE_0_TO_17 = (A & 0x0F) + 3;  // 3 to 18 bytes
   293→}
   294→```
   295→
   296→### Serial Routine Jump Table
   297→
   298→Located at `CPANEL_STATE_MACHINE_TABLE` (0xFC4489):
   299→
   300→| Offset | Routine | Address | Purpose |
   301→|--------|---------|---------|---------|
   302→| 0x00 | ROUTINE_0 | 0xFC47E9 | Idle state |
   303→| 0x04 | ROUTINE_1 | 0xFC44F9 | Start TX sequence |
   304→| 0x08 | ROUTINE_2 | 0xFC45A8 | Send LED data byte |
   305→| 0x0C | ROUTINE_3 | 0xFC4544 | Disable pins, next byte |
   306→| 0x10 | ROUTINE_4 | 0xFC460D | Continue LED data |
   307→| 0x14 | ROUTINE_5 | 0xFC4573 | Finalize LED group |
   308→| 0x18 | ROUTINE_6 | 0xFC4672 | Check for more data |
   309→| 0x1C | ROUTINE_0 | 0xFC47E9 | (duplicate) Idle |
   310→| 0x20 | ROUTINE_7 | 0xFC46EA | RX first byte |
   311→| 0x24 | ROUTINE_8 | 0xFC4767 | RX subsequent bytes |
   312→| 0x28 | ROUTINE_0 | 0xFC47E9 | (duplicate) Unreachable |
   313→
   314→## 5. HLE Implementation Guide
   315→
   316→### MAME Device Class Structure
   317→
   318→```cpp
   319→// kn5000_cpanel.h
   320→
   321→#ifndef MAME_TECHNICS_KN5000_CPANEL_H
   322→#define MAME_TECHNICS_KN5000_CPANEL_H
   323→
   324→#pragma once
   325→
   326→class kn5000_cpanel_device : public device_t
   327→{
   328→public:
   329→    kn5000_cpanel_device(const machine_config &mconfig, const char *tag, device_t *owner, uint32_t clock);
   330→
   331→    // Serial interface
   332→    void sin_w(int state);           // Serial data in (from main CPU)
   333→    int sout_r();                    // Serial data out (to main CPU)
   334→    void sclk_w(int state);          // Serial clock
   335→    void cntr_w(int state);          // Chip select / control
   336→
   337→    // Configuration
   338→    auto sout_callback() { return m_sout_cb.bind(); }

   340→
   341→protected:
   342→    virtual void device_start() override;
   343→    virtual void device_reset() override;
   344→    virtual ioport_constructor device_input_ports() const override;
   345→
   346→private:
   347→    // Serial state
   348→    uint8_t m_rx_shift;              // Receive shift register
   349→    uint8_t m_tx_shift;              // Transmit shift register

   352→
   353→    // Command processing
   354→    uint8_t m_cmd_buffer[2];         // 2-byte command buffer

   356→
   357→    // Panel state
   358→    uint8_t m_button_state[16];      // 16 segments * 8 buttons
   359→    uint8_t m_led_state[60];         // LED array (60 bytes)

   361→
   362→    // Callbacks
   363→    devcb_write_line m_sout_cb;
   364→    devcb_write_line m_irq_cb;
   365→
   366→    // Internal methods
   367→    void process_command();

   373→DECLARE_DEVICE_TYPE(KN5000_CPANEL, kn5000_cpanel_device)

   376→```
   377→
   378→### Key Callbacks to Implement
   379→
   380→```cpp
   381→// Command processing
   382→void kn5000_cpanel_device::process_command()
   383→{
   384→    uint8_t cmd = m_cmd_buffer[0];
   385→    uint8_t data = m_cmd_buffer[1];
   386→    uint8_t response[16];
   387→    int resp_len = 0;
   388→
   389→    // Determine packet type from high bits
   390→    bool is_right_panel = (cmd & 0xE0) >= 0x80;  // Bits 7-5 >= 4
   391→
   392→    switch (cmd)
   393→    {
   394→    // Initialization commands
   395→    case 0x1F:  // Init (left panel)
   396→    case 0x1D:
   397→    case 0x1E:
   398→    case 0xDD:  // Setup
   399→        // Acknowledge with sync packet
   400→        response[0] = 0x18 | (is_right_panel ? 0x80 : 0);  // Type 3 = sync
   401→        response[1] = 0x00;
   402→        resp_len = 2;
   403→        break;
   404→
   405→    // Query commands
   406→    case 0x20:  // Query left panel
   407→    case 0xE0:  // Query right panel
   408→        if (data == 0x00) {
   409→            // Ping - respond with sync
   410→            response[0] = 0x18;
   411→            response[1] = 0x00;
   412→            resp_len = 2;
   413→        } else if (data == 0x0B || data == 0x10) {
   414→            // Button state query
   415→            // NOTE: Panel selection is via bit 6, NOT the type field!
   416→            // Bit 6 = 0: right panel, Bit 6 = 1: left panel
   417→            int segment = data & 0x0F;
   418→            response[0] = (is_right_panel ? 0x00 : 0x40) | segment;  // Bit 6 for left panel
   419→            response[1] = get_button_segment(segment + (is_right_panel ? 0 : 16));
   420→            resp_len = 2;
   421→        }
   422→        break;
   423→
   424→    case 0x25:  // Left data command
   425→    case 0xE2:
   426→    case 0xE3:
   427→        // Extended data - respond appropriately
   428→        response[0] = 0x18;  // Sync
   429→        response[1] = data;
   430→        resp_len = 2;
   431→        break;
   432→
   433→    case 0x2B:  // Init state array (left)
   434→    case 0xEB:  // Init state array (right)
   435→        // Send all button segments
   436→        // NOTE: Bit 6 selects panel (0=right, 1=left)
   437→        for (int seg = 0; seg < 16; seg++) {
   438→            response[0] = seg | (is_right_panel ? 0x00 : 0x40);  // Bit 6 for left panel
   439→            response[1] = get_button_segment(seg + (is_right_panel ? 0 : 16));
   440→            send_response(response, 2);
   441→        }
   442→        return;
   443→    }
   444→
   445→    if (resp_len > 0) {
   446→        send_response(response, resp_len);
   447→    }
   448→}
   449→```

   496→### LED Control Interface
   497→
   498→LEDs are controlled via the `CPANEL_LED_TX_BUFFER` array (60 bytes at 0x8E01):
   499→
   500→```cpp
   501→void kn5000_cpanel_device::update_leds(int index, uint8_t pattern)
   502→{
   503→    // Index wraps at 0x3C (60)
   504→    index %= 60;
   505→    m_led_state[index] = pattern;
   506→
   507→    // Map LED index to physical LEDs
   508→    // The LED array is transmitted in 2-byte sequences
   509→    // Byte 0: Row select (bits 5-0 = row, bits 7-6 = panel select)
   510→    // Byte 1: Column pattern (which LEDs in row are lit)
   511→
   512→    // Update MAME output for visual feedback
   513→    for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; bit++) {
   514→        machine().output().set_indexed_value("led", index * 8 + bit, BIT(pattern, bit));
   515→    }
   516→}
   517→```

   544→### Rotary Encoder Format
   545→
   546→Encoders send signed delta values via Type 2 packets:
   547→
   548→```cpp
   549→void kn5000_cpanel_device::process_encoder(int encoder_id, int8_t delta)
   550→{
   551→    // Known Encoder IDs (from firmware analysis):
   552→    // 2: Data wheel / jog wheel -> ENCODER_0_OUTPUT
   553→    // 5: Volume slider / expression -> ENCODER_1_OUTPUT, MIDI_CC_VOLUME_VALUE
   554→    // Other IDs (0-1, 3-4, 6-31) return 0xFFFF (no handler)
   555→
   556→    m_encoder_delta[encoder_id] += delta;
   557→
   558→    // Report encoder change
   559→    // Byte 0 format: [ ID_hi[1:0] | 0 | 1 | 0 | ID_lo[2:0] ]
   560→    //                  bits 7-6     5   4   3   bits 2-0
   561→    // Type 2 = bits 5-3 = 010 = 0x10
   562→    uint8_t response[2];
   563→    response[0] = 0x10 | (encoder_id & 0x07) | ((encoder_id & 0x18) << 3);  // Type 2 + encoder ID
   564→    response[1] = delta;
   565→    send_response(response, 2);
   566→}
   567→```

   569→### MIDI Controller Output
   570→
   571→Encoder and analog input values are converted to MIDI Control Change messages and stored in RAM variables before being sent to the sound engine:
   572→
   573→**Controller Mapping:**
   574→
   575→| Variable | MIDI CC# | Controller Name |
   576→|----------|----------|-----------------|
   577→| `MIDI_CC_EXPRESSION_VALUE` | 0 | Bank Select MSB / Expression |
   578→| `MIDI_CC_MODWHEEL_VALUE` | 1 | Modulation Wheel |
   579→| `MIDI_CC_BREATH_VALUE` | 2 | Breath Controller |
   580→| `MIDI_CC_FOOT_VALUE` | 4 | Foot Controller |
   581→| `MIDI_CC_VOLUME_VALUE` | 7 | Volume (estimated) |
   582→
   583→**Change Detection:**
   584→
   585→The `*_PENDING` variants (e.g., `MIDI_CC_MODWHEEL_PENDING`) use bit 7 as a "value changed" flag:
   586→- When an encoder/ADC value changes, bit 7 is set
   587→- The MIDI output routine checks bit 7, sends the value if set, then clears bit 7
   588→- This prevents redundant MIDI messages for unchanged values
   589→
   590→**MIDI Message Format (at 0x9127-0x912A):**
   591→
   592→| Address | Field | Example |
   593→|---------|-------|---------|
   594→| 0x9127 | Status byte | 0xB0 (Control Change, channel 0) |
   595→| 0x9128 | Controller # | 0x01 (Modulation) |
   596→| 0x9129 | Value | 0x00-0x7F |
   597→| 0x912A | Velocity/Range | 0x7F |

Design an implementation plan for adding input support to the Another World VM running on the KN5000.

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

## MAME Input Ports (from kn5000.cpp)
The MAME driver has keyboard-mapped buttons. Relevant navigation buttons from the LEFT panel:

CPL_SEG7 (8 bits): RIGHT 4, RIGHT 5, DISPLAY_HOLD, EXIT, UP 7, DOWN 7, UP 8, DOWN 8
CPL_SEG8 (8 bits): RIGHT 1, RIGHT 2, RIGHT 3, (unused), UP 5, DOWN 5, UP 6, DOWN 6  
CPL_SEG9 (8 bits): LEFT 3, LEFT 4, LEFT 5, (unused), UP 3, DOWN 3, UP 4, DOWN 4
CPL_SEG10 (8 bits): LEFT 1, LEFT 2, HELP, OTHER_PARTS, UP 1, DOWN 1, UP 2, DOWN 2

These would need keyboard key bindings in MAME (arrow keys, space, etc.).

## Existing Code Structure
- `src/another_world_vm.asm`: VM implementation, ~2400 lines
- `src/main.asm`: Platform setup, RAM variables, timer ISR
- VM frame loop: MAIN_LOOP → EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION → ... → NEXT_THREAD → (back to MAIN_LOOP)
- `_write_vm_var`: Input A=index, DE=value
- PAUSE function polls SYSTEM_TICKS for frame timing
- NEXT_THREAD processes thread switching + part switching at frame boundaries

## Files to read for exact register addresses and protocol:
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.asm` for SFR addresses
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` for full protocol
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` and `.cpp` for what the MAME HLE expects
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/cpanel_routines.asm` for existing firmware button polling

## Design Requirements
1. Read control panel button state each frame
2. Map specific buttons to: Left, Right, Up, Down, Action
3. Update VM variables: 0xE5, 0xFA, 0xFB, 0xFC, 0xFD, 0xFE
4. Call input update from the VM frame loop (NEXT_THREAD area or PAUSE)
5. Must work in MAME testing; real hardware is a bonus

Please design a detailed implementation plan. Consider:
- How to initialize SC1 for cpanel communication
- How to poll buttons (blocking vs non-blocking, timing)
- Which specific buttons/segments to use for game controls
- How to structure the code (subroutines, where to call from)
- What RAM variables are needed
- Potential issues (timing, serial buffer, ISR needs)

Design an implementation plan for adding input support to the Another World VM running on the KN5000.

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

## MAME Input Ports (from kn5000.cpp)
The MAME driver has keyboard-mapped buttons. Relevant navigation buttons from the LEFT panel:

CPL_SEG7 (8 bits): RIGHT 4, RIGHT 5, DISPLAY_HOLD, EXIT, UP 7, DOWN 7, UP 8, DOWN 8
CPL_SEG8 (8 bits): RIGHT 1, RIGHT 2, RIGHT 3, (unused), UP 5, DOWN 5, UP 6, DOWN 6  
CPL_SEG9 (8 bits): LEFT 3, LEFT 4, LEFT 5, (unused), UP 3, DOWN 3, UP 4, DOWN 4
CPL_SEG10 (8 bits): LEFT 1, LEFT 2, HELP, OTHER_PARTS, UP 1, DOWN 1, UP 2, DOWN 2

These would need keyboard key bindings in MAME (arrow keys, space, etc.).

## Existing Code Structure
- `src/another_world_vm.asm`: VM implementation, ~2400 lines
- `src/main.asm`: Platform setup, RAM variables, timer ISR
- VM frame loop: MAIN_LOOP → EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION → ... → NEXT_THREAD → (back to MAIN_LOOP)
- `_write_vm_var`: Input A=index, DE=value
- PAUSE function polls SYSTEM_TICKS for frame timing
- NEXT_THREAD processes thread switching + part switching at frame boundaries

## Files to read for exact register addresses and protocol:
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.asm` for SFR addresses
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` for full protocol
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` and `.cpp` for what the MAME HLE expects
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/cpanel_routines.asm` for existing firmware button polling

## Design Requirements
1. Read control panel button state each frame
2. Map specific buttons to: Left, Right, Up, Down, Action
3. Update VM variables: 0xE5, 0xFA, 0xFB, 0xFC, 0xFD, 0xFE
4. Call input update from the VM frame loop (NEXT_THREAD area or PAUSE)
5. Must work in MAME testing; real hardware is a bonus

Please design a detailed implementation plan. Consider:
- How to initialize SC1 for cpanel communication
- How to poll buttons (blocking vs non-blocking, timing)
- Which specific buttons/segments to use for game controls
- How to structure the code (subroutines, where to call from)
- What RAM variables are needed
- Potential issues (timing, serial buffer, ISR needs)

Read the relevant files mentioned above to get exact register addresses and protocol details.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

Design an implementation plan for adding input support to the Another World VM running on the KN5000.

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

## MAME Input Ports (from kn5000.cpp)
The MAME driver has keyboard-mapped buttons. Relevant navigation buttons from the LEFT panel:

CPL_SEG7 (8 bits): RIGHT 4, RIGHT 5, DISPLAY_HOLD, EXIT, UP 7, DOWN 7, UP 8, DOWN 8
CPL_SEG8 (8 bits): RIGHT 1, RIGHT 2, RIGHT 3, (unused), UP 5, DOWN 5, UP 6, DOWN 6  
CPL_SEG9 (8 bits): LEFT 3, LEFT 4, LEFT 5, (unused), UP 3, DOWN 3, UP 4, DOWN 4
CPL_SEG10 (8 bits): LEFT 1, LEFT 2, HELP, OTHER_PARTS, UP 1, DOWN 1, UP 2, DOWN 2

These would need keyboard key bindings in MAME (arrow keys, space, etc.).

## Existing Code Structure
- `src/another_world_vm.asm`: VM implementation, ~2400 lines
- `src/main.asm`: Platform setup, RAM variables, timer ISR
- VM frame loop: MAIN_LOOP → EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION → ... → NEXT_THREAD → (back to MAIN_LOOP)
- `_write_vm_var`: Input A=index, DE=value
- PAUSE function polls SYSTEM_TICKS for frame timing
- NEXT_THREAD processes thread switching + part switching at frame boundaries

## Files to read for exact register addresses and protocol:
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.asm` for SFR addresses
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` for full protocol
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` and `.cpp` for what the MAME HLE expects
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/cpanel_routines.asm` for existing firmware button polling

## Design Requirements
1. Read control panel button state each frame
2. Map specific buttons to: Left, Right, Up, Down, Action
3. Update VM variables: 0xE5, 0xFA, 0xFB, 0xFC, 0xFD, 0xFE
4. Call input update from the VM frame loop (NEXT_THREAD area or PAUSE)
5. Must work in MAME testing; real hardware is a bonus

Please design a detailed implementation plan. Consider:
- How to initialize SC1 for cpanel communication
- How to poll buttons (blocking vs non-blocking, timing)
- Which specific buttons/segments to use for game controls
- How to structure the code (subroutines, where to call from)
- What RAM variables are needed
- Potential issues (timing, serial buffer, ISR needs)

Read the relevant files mentioned above to get exact register addresses and protocol details.

Design an implementation plan for adding input support to the Another World VM running on the KN5000.

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
```

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

## MAME Input Ports (from kn5000.cpp)
The MAME driver has keyboard-mapped buttons. Relevant navigation buttons from the LEFT panel:

CPL_SEG7 (8 bits): RIGHT 4, RIGHT 5, DISPLAY_HOLD, EXIT, UP 7, DOWN 7, UP 8, DOWN 8
CPL_SEG8 (8 bits): RIGHT 1, RIGHT 2, RIGHT 3, (unused), UP 5, DOWN 5, UP 6, DOWN 6  
CPL_SEG9 (8 bits): LEFT 3, LEFT 4, LEFT 5, (unused), UP 3, DOWN 3, UP 4, DOWN 4
CPL_SEG10 (8 bits): LEFT 1, LEFT 2, HELP, OTHER_PARTS, UP 1, DOWN 1, UP 2, DOWN 2

These would need keyboard key bindings in MAME (arrow keys, space, etc.).

Design an implementation plan for adding input support to the Another World VM running on the KN5000.

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

## MAME Input Ports (from kn5000.cpp)
The MAME driver has keyboard-mapped buttons. Relevant navigation buttons from the LEFT panel:

CPL_SEG7 (8 bits): RIGHT 4, RIGHT 5, DISPLAY_HOLD, EXIT, UP 7, DOWN 7, UP 8, DOWN 8
CPL_SEG8 (8 bits): RIGHT 1, RIGHT 2, RIGHT 3, (unused), UP 5, DOWN 5, UP 6, DOWN 6  
CPL_SEG9 (8 bits): LEFT 3, LEFT 4, LEFT 5, (unused), UP 3, DOWN 3, UP 4, DOWN 4
CPL_SEG10 (8 bits): LEFT 1, LEFT 2, HELP, OTHER_PARTS, UP 1, DOWN 1, UP 2, DOWN 2

These would need keyboard key bindings in MAME (arrow keys, space, etc.).

## Existing Code Structure
- `src/another_world_vm.asm`: VM implementation, ~2400 lines
- `src/main.asm`: Platform setup, RAM variables, timer ISR
- VM frame loop: MAIN_LOOP → EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION → ... → NEXT_THREAD → (back to MAIN_LOOP)
- `_write_vm_var`: Input A=index, DE=value
- PAUSE function polls SYSTEM_TICKS for frame timing
- NEXT_THREAD processes thread switching + part switching at frame boundaries

## Files to read for exact register addresses and protocol:
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.asm` for SFR addresses
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` for full protocol
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` and `.cpp` for what the MAME HLE expects
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/cpanel_routines.asm` for existing firmware button polling

## Design Requirements
1. Read control panel button state each frame
2. Map specific buttons to: Left, Right, Up, Down, Action
3. Update VM variables: 0xE5, 0xFA, 0xFB, 0xFC, 0xFD, 0xFE
4. Call input update from the VM frame loop (NEXT_THREAD area or PAUSE)
5. Must work in MAME testing; real hardware is a bonus

Please design a detailed implementation plan. Consider:
- How to initialize SC1 for cpanel communication
- How to poll buttons (blocking vs non-blocking, timing)
- Which specific buttons/segments to use for game controls
- How to structure the code (subroutines, where to call from)
- What RAM variables are needed
- Potential issues (timing, serial buffer, ISR needs)

Read the relevant files mentioned above to get exact register addresses and protocol details.

Design an implementation plan for adding input support to the Another World VM running on the KN5000.

## Context

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
    write_vm_variable(0xFA, button);  // action
    write_vm_variable(0xFE, m);       // action + position mask
}
```

## MAME Input Ports (from kn5000.cpp)
The MAME driver has keyboard-mapped buttons. Relevant navigation buttons from the LEFT panel:

CPL_SEG7 (8 bits): RIGHT 4, RIGHT 5, DISPLAY_HOLD, EXIT, UP 7, DOWN 7, UP 8, DOWN 8
CPL_SEG8 (8 bits): RIGHT 1, RIGHT 2, RIGHT 3, (unused), UP 5, DOWN 5, UP 6, DOWN 6  
CPL_SEG9 (8 bits): LEFT 3, LEFT 4, LEFT 5, (unused), UP 3, DOWN 3, UP 4, DOWN 4
CPL_SEG10 (8 bits): LEFT 1, LEFT 2, HELP, OTHER_PARTS, UP 1, DOWN 1, UP 2, DOWN 2

These would need keyboard key bindings in MAME (arrow keys, space, etc.).

## Existing Code Structure
- `src/another_world_vm.asm`: VM implementation, ~2400 lines
- `src/main.asm`: Platform setup, RAM variables, timer ISR
- VM frame loop: MAIN_LOOP → EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION → ... → NEXT_THREAD → (back to MAIN_LOOP)
- `_write_vm_var`: Input A=index, DE=value
- PAUSE function polls SYSTEM_TICKS for frame timing
- NEXT_THREAD processes thread switching + part switching at frame boundaries

## Files to read for exact register addresses and protocol:
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.asm` for SFR addresses
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-docs/control-panel-protocol.md` for full protocol
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000_cpanel.h` and `.cpp` for what the MAME HLE expects
- `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/maincpu/cpanel_routines.asm` for existing firmware button polling

## Design Requirements
1. Read control panel button state each frame
2. Map specific buttons to: Left, Right, Up, Down, Action
3. Update VM variables: 0xE5, 0xFA, 0xFB, 0xFC, 0xFD, 0xFE
4. Call input update from the VM frame loop (NEXT_THREAD area or PAUSE)
5. Must work in MAME testing; real hardware is a bonus

Please design a detailed implementation plan. Consider:
- How to initialize SC1 for cpanel communication
- How to poll buttons (blocking vs non-blocking, timing)
- Which specific buttons/segments to use for game controls
- How to structure the code (subroutines, where to call from)
- What RAM variables are needed
- Potential issues (timing, serial buffer, ISR needs)

Read the relevant files mentioned above to get exact register addresses and protocol details.

1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs

```cpp
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP

        ud = -1; m |= 8;

        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);

    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
```

The Another World VM needs player input (Up/Down/Left/Right + Action button) to play the game. Currently all input VM variables stay at 0 (neutral). The VM runs as bare-metal TLCS-900 assembly replacing the KN5000 firmware.

## Hardware Architecture

The KN5000 control panel buttons communicate via SC1 serial port (UART) through two panel MCUs (CPL/CPR). The buttons are NOT memory-mapped - they require serial request/response protocol.

In MAME, the `kn5000_cpanel` HLE device:
1. Receives serial commands on SC1 TX
2. Reads from MAME input ports (CPR_SEG0-10, CPL_SEG0-10)
3. Responds with button state packets on SC1 RX

## SC1 Serial Port Registers (TMP94C241F SFR)
- SC1BUF (0xD8): Data buffer
- SC1CR (0xD9): Control register
- SC1MOD (0xDA): Mode register  
- BR1CR (0xDB): Baud rate control

## Control Panel Protocol (from kn5000-docs)
- Baud rates: 31.25 kHz (init), 250 kHz (normal)
- Query command: 2 bytes (e.g., 0x20 0x00 for right panel status)
- Response: variable-length packets with (segment_index, button_bitmap) pairs
- Format: 8-bit, async, no parity

## Reference HLE input_updatePlayer (from aw_hle.cpp lines 121-177)
```cpp
void another_world_cpu_device::input_updatePlayer() {
    int16_t lr = 0, m = 0, ud = 0;
    int8_t input = m_read_input();  // 8-bit input port
    
    write_vm_variable(0xDA, m_read_keyboard());  // last keychar
    
    if (BIT(input, 4) && partId != PART(0) && partId != PART(9))
        requestedNextPart = GAME_PART(9);  // return to password screen
    
    if (BIT(input, 2)) { lr = 1; m |= 1; }   // RIGHT
    if (BIT(input, 3)) { lr = -1; m |= 2; }   // LEFT
    if (BIT(input, 0)) { ud = 1; m |= 4; }    // DOWN
    if (BIT(input, 1)) {                        // UP
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, -1);
        ud = -1; m |= 8;
    } else {
        write_vm_variable(0xE5, ud);
    }
    
    write_vm_variable(0xFB, ud);    // jump/down
    write_vm_variable(0xFC, lr);    // left/right
    write_vm_variable(0xFD, m);     // position mask (note: code uses 0xFA in header but actual is 0xFD)
    
    int16_t button = 0;
    if (BIT(input, 7)) { button = 1; m |= 0x80; }
```

; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>

;
; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
;
; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
;
; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
; as a high-level emulation on MAME
;
; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
;
; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
;
; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
; using the scripts provided at:
; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
;
; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh
TICKS_PER_SLICE		EQU 250		; ~20ms at 12500 Hz tick rate (80 µs/tick)

CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte

FROZEN	EQU 0
NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh

; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
; MAINCPU: in DRAM at 0x020000-0x05FFFF
; EXTENSION: in extension board SRAM at 0x240000-0x27FFFF
	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 020000h
PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 030000h
PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 040000h
PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 050000h
	endif
	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h
	endif

; VM variable indices (used by the game engine)
VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED		EQU 03Ch
VM_VARIABLE_LAST_KEYCHAR	EQU 0C5h
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN	EQU 0E5h
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN	EQU 0DCh
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT	EQU 0E9h
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK	EQU 0FAh
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION		EQU 0FBh
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK EQU 0FBh
VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y		EQU 0F9h

; Game part IDs (from reference: parts.h)
GAME_PART_FIRST			EQU 03E80h
GAME_PART_PROTECTION	EQU 03E80h	; Part 0: Copy protection
GAME_PART_INTRO			EQU 03E81h	; Part 1: Introduction cinematic
GAME_PART_WATER			EQU 03E82h	; Part 2: Water / lake
GAME_PART_JAIL			EQU 03E83h	; Part 3: Jail / prison
GAME_PART_CITADEL		EQU 03E84h	; Part 4: Citadel
GAME_PART_BATTLECHAR	EQU 03E85h	; Part 5: Battle cinematic
GAME_PART_ARENA			EQU 03E86h	; Part 6: Arena
GAME_PART_FINAL			EQU 03E87h	; Part 7: Final / ending
GAME_PART_PASSWORD1		EQU 03E88h	; Part 8: Password entry
GAME_PART_PASSWORD2		EQU 03E89h	; Part 9: Password entry (alt)
GAME_PART_LAST			EQU 03E89h
GAME_NUM_PARTS			EQU 10
NUM_MEM_LIST			EQU 091h

CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN:
	; int16_t xmax = MAX(x1, x2);
	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP GT, XMAX_OK
	LD WA, (X2)

	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP LT, XMIN_OK
	LD WA, (X2)
XMIN_OK:
	LD (LINE_XMIN), WA
	RET

; boot_hw_init.asm - Minimal Hardware Initialization (Local)
; =============================================================================
; Minimal version of the shared boot_hw_init.asm from kn5000-roms-disasm.
; Only includes what's needed for: display (VGA + VRAM) and serial (SC0).
;
; Removed from original (315 bytes):
;   - Port F setup (control panel / MIDI via SC1)
;   - 8-bit timer setup (T01, T23)
;   - 16-bit timer setup (T4, T5)
;   - Interrupt mode control (IIMC)
;
; Kept but potentially removable (marked with REVIEW):
;   - Data bus port setup (P2, P3, P7) - may be needed for external bus
;   - Address bus port setup (PA-PH, PZ) - may be needed for VRAM/VGA access
;   - Block chip select config (B0-B5) - may be needed for bus timing
;   These are safe to keep but could be tested for removal in MAME.
; =============================================================================

	; === Watchdog Timer Disable ===
	LD (WDMOD), 000h
	LD (WDCR), 0b1h

	; === System Clock Setup ===
	LD (CLKMOD), 004h			; High-speed (16 MHz)

	; === Data Bus Ports Setup (P2, P3, P7) ===
	; REVIEW: May be needed for external bus access to VGA/VRAM
	LD (P2FC), 0ffh
	LD (P3FC), 0ffh
	LD (P7), 0ffh
	LD (P7FC), 01fh
	LD (P7CR), 000h

	; === Address Bus Ports Setup (PA, PB, PC, PD, PE, PH, PZ) ===
	; REVIEW: May be needed for address lines to reach 0x170000 (VGA)
	; and 0x1A0000 (VRAM). Safe to keep; test removal in MAME.
	LD (PA), 0feh
	LD (PAFC), 008h
	LD (PB), 0ffh
	LD (PBFC), 01fh
	LD (PC), 003h
	LD (PCFC), 000h
	LD (PCCR), 002h
	LD (PD), 000h
	LD (PDFC), 006h
	LD (PDCR), 011h
	LD (PE), 000h
	LD (PEFC), 042h
	LD (PECR), 020h
	LD (PH), 000h
	LD (PHFC), 01eh
	LD (PHCR), 009h
	LD (PZ), 0ffh
	LD (PZCR), 003h

	; === Memory Controller: Start Address Registers ===
	LD (MSAR0), 01eh			; Block 0 @ 0x1E0000
	LD (MSAR1), 010h			; Block 1 @ 0x100000 (VGA at 0x170000)
	LD (MSAR2), 0c0h			; Block 2 @ 0xC00000
	LD (MSAR3), 000h			; Block 3 @ 0x000000 (DRAM)
	LD (MSAR4), 080h			; Block 4 @ 0x800000
	LD (MSAR5), 000h			; Block 5 @ 0x000000

	; === Memory Controller: Address Mask Registers ===
	LD (MAMR0), 00fh
	LD (MAMR1), 03fh
	LD (MAMR2), 07fh
	LD (MAMR3), 01fh
	LD (MAMR4), 0ffh
	LD (MAMR5), 0ffh

	LD (P8), 03bh
	LD (P8FC), 07fh
	LD (P8CR), 03fh

   138→void kn5000_state::maincpu_mem(address_map &map)
   139→{
   140→	map(0x000000, 0x0fffff).ram().share("nvram1"); // 1Mbyte = 2 * 4Mbit DRAMs @ IC9, IC10 (CS3)
   141→	// Button states and LED control are now handled via serial protocol to cpanel HLE device
   142→	//FIXME: map(0x110000, 0x11ffff).m(m_fdc, FUNC(upd765a_device::map)); // Floppy Controller @ IC208
   143→	//FIXME: map(0x120000, 0x12ffff).w(m_fdc, FUNC(upd765a_device::dack_w)); // Floppy DMA Acknowledge
   144→	map(0x140000, 0x14ffff).r(m_maincpu_latch, FUNC(generic_latch_8_device::read)); // @ IC23
   145→	map(0x140000, 0x14ffff).w(m_subcpu_latch, FUNC(generic_latch_8_device::write)); // @ IC22
   146→	map(0x1703b0, 0x1703df).m("vga", FUNC(mn89304_vga_device::io_map)); // LCD controller @ IC206
   147→	map(0x1a0000, 0x1dffff).rw("vga", FUNC(mn89304_vga_device::mem_linear_r), FUNC(mn89304_vga_device::mem_linear_w));
   148→	map(0x1e0000, 0x1fffff).ram().share("nvram2"); // 1Mbit SRAM @ IC21 (CS0)  Note: I think this is the message "ERROR in back-up SRAM"
   149→	map(0x300000, 0x3fffff).rom().region("custom_data", 0); // 8MBit FLASH ROM @ IC19 (CS5)
   150→	map(0x400000, 0x7fffff).rom().region("rhythm_data", 0); // 32MBit ROM @ IC14 (A22=1 and CS5)
   151→	//map(0x800000, 0x82ffff).rom().region("subprogram", 0); // not sure yet in which chip this is stored, but I suspect it should be IC19
   152→	map(0x800000, 0x9fffff).mirror(0x200000).rom().region("table_data", 0); //2 * 8MBit ROMs @ IC1, IC3 (CS2)
   153→	map(0xe00000, 0xffffff).mask(0x1fffff).rom().region("program", 0); //2 * 8MBit FLASH ROMs @ IC4, IC6
   154→}
   155→
   156→void kn5000_state::subcpu_mem(address_map &map)
   157→{
   158→	// There seems to also be devices at 110000, 130000 and 1e0000
   159→
   160→	map(0x000000, 0x0fffff).ram(); // 1Mbyte = 2 * 4Mbit DRAMs @ IC28, IC29
   161→	//map(0x110000, 0x11????).rw(FUNC(kn5000_state::tone_generator_r), FUNC(kn5000_state::tone_generator_w)); // @ IC303
   162→	map(0x120000, 0x12ffff).r(m_subcpu_latch, FUNC(generic_latch_8_device::read)); // @ IC22
   163→	map(0x120000, 0x12ffff).w(m_maincpu_latch, FUNC(generic_latch_8_device::write)); // @ IC23
   164→	//map(0x130000, 0x13????).rw(FUNC(kn5000_state::dsp1_r), FUNC(kn5000_state::dsp1_w)); // @ IC311
   165→	map(0xfe0000, 0xffffff).rom().region("subcpu", 0); // 1Mbit MASK ROM @ IC30
   166→
   167→	//Note:
   168→	// DSP2 @ IC302 uses a serial #0 pins but I think it is bitbanging those pins.
   169→}
